items.cn: delere 意为毁灭或抹去。

items.en: Deletio named the act of wiping out.
items.cn: deletio 指抹去这一行为。

items.en: Deletion entered English for striking out text.

items.en: Editors used it for cuts in a manuscript.
items.cn: 编辑用它指手稿上的删节。

items.en: It became the standard word for removing files.

definition_zh: 意识形态的；观念体系的；带有政治立场的；教条化的
definition_en: relating to a system of ideas and beliefs, especially one that shapes political or social action
core_image: 一副有色眼镜：同样的世界，透过它只剩一种颜色
scene: 这里指「意识形态的」。 The debate was settled on ideological grounds long before any data were examined.
sceneCN: 这里 ideological 是「以观念体系为根据的」（第 2 个义项：政策与判断建立在信念体系上）；句意：这场争论早在检查任何数据之前，就按意识形态立场定下了。图中可辨识物件：两把对立摆放的椅子、标着两种颜色的旗子、被推到一旁的图表。

pos.zh: 意识形态的；观念体系的；带政治色彩的

derivatives.zh: 意识形态拥护者；理论空谈者

senses.title: Belonging to a system of ideas
senses.definition: relating to a structured set of ideas about how society should work
senses.definitionCN: 与社会应如何运转的一整套观念相关的
senses.example: The two camps are separated by an ideological wall.
senses.exampleCN: 两个阵营被一堵意识形态的墙隔开。
senses.why: Ideology was coined as the 'science of ideas'. Its adjective simply says that something belongs to that layer of thought rather than to facts.
senses.whyCN: ideology 当初被造为“观念的科学”。其形容词只是说明某物属于思想这一层，而不属于事实层。

senses.title: Founded on belief rather than evidence
senses.definition: based on a set of beliefs that is accepted in advance of evidence
senses.definitionCN: 建立在先于证据就被接受的信念之上的
senses.example: The reform was ideological rather than practical.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革是意识形态驱动的，而非出于实际需要。
senses.why: The word marks the point where a conclusion comes from a creed instead of a measurement. Belief is placed at the front of the sentence.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标记了一个转折点：结论来自信条而非测量。信念被放到了句子的最前面。

senses.title: Doctrinaire, in a critical tone
senses.definition: used critically to mean driven by doctrine and closed to contrary facts
senses.definitionCN: 带批评意味，指被教条驱动、对相反事实封闭
senses.example: Critics dismissed the plan as purely ideological.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者把该计划斥为纯属教条。
senses.why: Napoleon turned the word ideology into a sneer two centuries ago. The adjective inherited that sneer and can now accuse someone of preferring theory to reality.
senses.whyCN: 两百年前拿破仑把 ideology 变成了讥讽语。这个形容词继承了那种讥讽，如今可以指责任某人宁可要理论也不要现实。

senses.title: Carrying a clear political colour
senses.definition: showing a recognizable political alignment in content or tone
senses.definitionCN: 在内容或语气上显出可辨识的政治归属
senses.example: The newspaper has a clear ideological line.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报纸有明确的意识形态路线。
senses.why: A 'line' is the visual form of the word: ideas arranged along one direction, so that readers can see which side a text stands on.
senses.whyCN: “路线”是这个词的可视形态：观念沿一个方向排开，读者因此看得出文本站在哪一边。

senses.title: Belonging to the early study of ideas
senses.titleCN: 观念学意义上的（学术史）
senses.definition: in the history of thought, relating to the project of analysing the origin of ideas
senses.definitionCN: 在思想史中，与分析观念起源的学术计划相关的
senses.example: The term first appears in the ideological writings of the 1790s.
senses.exampleCN: 该词最早出现在 18 世纪 90 年代的观念学著作中。
senses.why: Destutt de Tracy wanted a natural science of ideas. The adjective still carries that cool, analytical tone when historians use it.
senses.whyCN: 德斯蒂·德·特拉西想建立一门关于观念的自然科学。历史学者使用这个形容词时，仍带着那种冷静的分析语气。

senses.title: Expressing cultural values
senses.definition: encoding the values and assumptions of a culture rather than being neutral
senses.definitionCN: 编码了某种文化的价值与预设，而非中立
senses.example: Textbooks are never ideologically neutral.
senses.exampleCN: 教科书从来不是意识形态中立的。
senses.why: The word is used to deny neutrality: what looks like plain description already carries a set of values, as a lens carries a tint.
senses.whyCN: 这个词被用来否认中立：看似平直的描述其实已经带着一套价值，就像镜片带着颜色。

senses.title: Serving to mobilize support
senses.definition: used to rally people around a cause or to justify a political programme
senses.definitionCN: 用来围绕某个事业动员群众或为政治纲领辩护的
senses.example: The broadcast served an ideological purpose more than a news one.
senses.exampleCN: 这档广播更多服务于宣传目的，而非新闻目的。
senses.why: Here ideas become a tool. The adjective names the function of the message rather than its content.
senses.whyCN: 这里的观念变成了工具。这个形容词命名的是讯息的功能，而不是其内容。

senses.title: A difference of theory, not of persons
senses.definition: describing a disagreement that rests on theory rather than personal feeling
senses.definitionCN: 描述建立在理论而非个人情感之上的分歧
senses.example: Their quarrel was ideological, not personal.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的争执是观念层面的，不是私人恩怨。
senses.why: The sentence uses the adjective to move a conflict up one level, from faces to frameworks, where it can be argued instead of felt.
senses.whyCN: 这句话用这个形容词把冲突抬高一层，从面孔升到框架，使它可以被辩论而不只是被感受。

intro.en: Ideological descends from a word invented in Paris in 1796. Destutt de Tracy joined Greek idea 'form, appearance' to -logia 'study' and called his project idéologie, the science of ideas. Napoleon turned the name into an insult, and the adjective inherited both the analytical and the sneering tone.
intro.cn: ideological 源于 1796 年巴黎造出的一个词。德斯蒂·德·特拉西把希腊语 idea“形相、外观”与 -logia“研究”结合，称自己的计划为 idéologie，即观念的科学。拿破仑把这个名称变成骂人的话，形容词同时继承了分析语气与讥讽语气。

items.en: The Greek verb idein, 'to see', is generally traced to a root reconstructed as *weyd-, 'to see, to know', which also underlies Latin videre and English wit.
items.cn: 希腊语动词 idein“看见”一般被追溯到重构词根 *weyd-“看见、知道”，它也是拉丁语 videre 与英语 wit 的来源。

items.en: Idea meant 'form, shape, appearance', then in Plato 'the eternal form perceived by the mind'. The visual origin is still audible in the word.
items.cn: idea 意为“形相、形状、外观”，在柏拉图那里指“由心智观看到的永恒形式”。视觉来源至今仍能从词里听出来。

items.en: -Logia, from logos 'word, account, reasoned discourse', built names for fields of study. Joined to idea it produced a 'study of ideas'.
items.cn: -logia 来自 logos“言说、论述、理性话语”，用于构成学科名称。与 idea 结合，就产生“关于观念的研究”。

items.en: Destutt de Tracy coined idéologie for a proposed science that would trace ideas to sensations. He meant it as neutral physiology of thought.
items.cn: 德斯蒂·德·特拉西造出 idéologie，指一门把观念追溯到感觉的科学。他本意是价值中立的思维生理学。

items.en: Napoleon mocked the idéologues as empty theorists, and the word spread with that stain. English took ideological in the early 19th century with both meanings alive.
items.cn: 拿破仑嘲笑这些观念学者是空谈理论家，这个词便带着这层污迹传播开来。英语在 19 世纪初借入 ideological 时，两种含义都还活着。

items.en: Political science generalized the adjective to any belief system that guides action. The neutral and the critical uses now sit side by side.
items.cn: 政治学把这个形容词推广到任何指导行动的信念体系。中立用法与批评用法如今并列存在。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the noun, the person and the adjective built on idea. The meaning group compares words about belief, doctrine and political alignment.
note.cn: 形近组区分 idea 词基上的名词、人物名词与形容词；词义组比较表示信念、教义与政治归属的词。

entries.definition: a system of ideas and beliefs, especially one that guides political action. It is the thing the adjective describes.
entries.definitionCN: 一套观念与信念，尤指指导政治行动的体系。它正是形容词所描述的对象。

entries.definition: a person who holds and defends a rigid set of ideas. It names a believer, not a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 坚持并捍卫一套僵硬观念的人。它指信奉者本人，而非性质。

entries.definition: perfect, or a standard of perfection. It shares the 'form' root but means excellence, not a political creed.
entries.definitionCN: 完美的，或完美的标准。它与“形相”词根同源，但指卓越，而非政治信条。

entries.definition: relating to government, parties or the distribution of power. It is broader: a policy can be political without resting on a creed.
entries.definitionCN: 与政府、政党或权力分配有关的。它更宽：一项政策可以是政治的，却不必建立在信条上。

entries.definition: relating to an official body of teaching, especially in religion. It stresses authorized teaching, while ideological stresses a social creed.
entries.definitionCN: 与官方教导体系有关的，尤指宗教。它强调被认可的教义，而 ideological 强调社会信条。

entries.definition: strongly attached to one party or cause. It adds loyalty to the idea, where ideological may be merely descriptive.
entries.definitionCN: 坚定附属于某一党派或事业的。它在观念之外加上忠诚，而 ideological 可能只是描述性的。

entries.definition: relating to philosophy or to a calm attitude to life. It points to reasoned inquiry, not to a programme of action.
entries.definitionCN: 与哲学有关的，或指对生活的平静态度。它指向理性探究，而非行动纲领。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build ideological from idea plus -logy, then let the tinted-lens image cover policy, textbooks, broadcasts and personal quarrels.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩从 idea 加 -logy 搭起 ideological，再用“有色镜片”意象覆盖政策、教科书、广播与私人争执。

normal.en: See idea + -logical: a logic built on ideas rather than on data.
normal.cn: 看成 idea 加 logical：一套建立在观念而非数据上的逻辑。

normal.en: Picture tinted glasses: the world is unchanged, but everything looks one colour.
normal.cn: 想象有色眼镜：世界没变，但一切都成了一个颜色。

normal.en: When a report explains facts, it is descriptive; when it starts from a creed, it is ideological.
normal.cn: 报告解释事实时是描述性的；从信条出发时就是意识形态的。

normal.en: Remember Napoleon's sneer: the word can be a neutral label or a sharp accusation.
normal.cn: 记住拿破仑的讥讽：这个词既可以是中立标签，也可以是尖锐指责。

normal.en: Link it to the pair: ideology is the system, ideological is the quality, ideologue is the person.
normal.cn: 连成一组：ideology 是体系，ideological 是性质，ideologue 是人。

abstract.en: Keep one image: a frame placed over the world before anything is allowed to be seen.
abstract.cn: 只记一个意象：在看世界之前，先罩上一个框架。

abstract.en: Treat the word as a warning that the explanation arrived before the evidence.
abstract.cn: 把这个词当作一个提醒：解释先于证据到达。

abstract.en: Notice that the same word can describe and accuse; only context decides which.
abstract.cn: 注意同一个词既能描述也能指责，只有语境决定是哪一种。

examples.en: The split in the party was ideological rather than personal.
examples.cn: 该党的分裂是意识形态上的，而非私人恩怨。

examples.en: Any curriculum carries an ideological load, however neutral it looks.
examples.cn: 任何课程都承担着意识形态负荷，无论它看起来多中立。

examples.en: They refused the offer for purely ideological reasons.
examples.cn: 他们纯因意识形态理由拒绝了这项提议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“爱迪优乐极可”：爱迪生式的乐观逻辑推到极致，就成了只讲观念的 ideological。

root: 法语 idéologie（1796 年德斯蒂·德·特拉西造词），由希腊语 ἰδέα“形相、外观”（来自 idein 看见）加 -λογία“学科”构成；形容词 ideological 由 idéologie 加 -al 派生，19 世纪初进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The word began as the name of a science of ideas and became a label for any creed that guides action. Its eight senses move from neutral membership ('belonging to a system of ideas') to sharp criticism ('doctrinaire'). What stays constant is the image of a frame placed in front of the world: the frame can be a research programme, a party line, a textbook's assumptions or a sneer.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词起初是一门观念科学的名称，后来成了任何指导行动的信条之名。八个义项从中立的归属（“属于一套观念”）一路走到尖锐批评（“教条化”）。不变的是“框架挡在世界之前”的意象：这个框架可以是研究计划、党派路线、教科书的预设，也可以是一声讥讽。

core.en: A frame of ideas standing between a person and the facts.
core.cn: 一套观念框架，立在人与事实之间。

branches.en: ORIGIN: the study of ideas and its neutral, analytical use.
branches.cn: 起源：观念之学及其中立、分析的用法。

branches.en: BASIS: conclusions drawn from belief, and disputes argued on theory.
branches.cn: 根据：从信念得出的结论，以及按理论争论的分歧。

branches.en: CRITICISM: doctrine closed to contrary facts.
branches.cn: 批评：对相反事实封闭的教条。

branches.en: POLITICS: a line taken, a message used to rally support.
branches.cn: 政治：选定的路线，以及用来动员支持的讯息。

branches.en: CULTURE: values carried by texts that look neutral.
branches.cn: 文化：看似中立的文本所携带的价值。

intro.en: Ideological is idea plus the combining form -logical. The items below show the noun, the person and the neutral adjective that share the same Greek base, and show how far the 'study' suffix spreads.
intro.cn: ideological 是 idea 加组合形式 -logical。下列条目展示共享同一希腊词基的名词、人物名词与中性形容词，并展示“学科”后缀扩散得有多远。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries are few because the word was coined in French from Greek parts. Latin idea is itself a borrowing of Greek ἰδέα, which is exactly the point: the concept travelled through Latin without a Latin root of its own.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目较少，因为这个词是法语用希腊成分造的。拉丁语 idea 本身就是希腊语 ἰδέα 的借词，这恰恰说明了要点：这个概念经由拉丁语传递，却没有自己的拉丁词根。

items.meaning: relating to a system of ideas
items.example: The conflict has an ideological dimension.
items.exampleCN: 这场冲突有意识形态维度。

items.meaning: a system of ideas and beliefs
items.example: The party's ideology has changed since the 1980s.
items.exampleCN: 该党的意识形态自 1980 年代以来已改变。

items.meaning: a rigid defender of a doctrine
items.example: He was a party ideologue rather than a manager.
items.exampleCN: 他是党的理论家，而不是管理者。

items.meaning: a thought or a mental form
items.example: The idea came to her in the shower.
items.exampleCN: 这个想法是她在淋浴时想到的。

items.example: The design aims at an ideal of simplicity.
items.exampleCN: 这个设计追求一种简洁的理想。

items.meaning: the belief that reality is grounded in mind
items.meaningCN: 认为实在以心灵为基础的信念
items.exampleCN: 德国唯心主义重塑了哲学。

items.meaning: from the standpoint of a belief system
items.exampleCN: 这家报纸在意识形态上有明确承诺。

items.meaning: relating to the forming of ideas
items.example: Ideational fluency is tested by listing uses.
items.exampleCN: 观念流畅性通过列举用途来测试。

latinEntries.meaning: existing in idea or ideal form
latinEntries.meaningCN: 存在于观念或理想形态中的

definition_zh: 合金化：把一种或多种元素加入金属熔体，以改变其强度、耐蚀性、导电性等性能的工艺
definition_en: the process of adding one or more elements to a metal so as to change its strength, corrosion resistance or other properties
core_image: 炉前工人用长钳夹起一小块银亮金属，压入翻涌的铜液，成分记录随之改写
scene: 炉前工人用长钳夹起一小块银亮金属，压入翻涌的铜液，成分记录随之改写。 Alloying raises the strength of aluminium without making it much heavier.
sceneCN: 这里指合金化这一工艺（第 1 个义项：向金属中加入元素以改变性能的过程）；句意为合金化提高了铝的强度，却没有让它重太多。

pos.zh: 合金化（工艺或过程，不可数）
一次合金化操作（可数，少见）

collocations.zh: 合金添加（加入的元素量）

derivatives.zh: alloy + -ed（分词形容词）→ 已合金化的，语义偏移为「含有加入元素的」
micro-（微量）+ alloying → 微合金化，语义偏移为「只加极少量元素来改善性能」
de-（去除）+ alloying → 脱合金，语义偏移为「选择性溶去某一元素」
alloying + element（元素）→ 合金元素，语义偏移为「为改性能而有意加入的元素」
alloy（合金；熔合）+ -ing → 合金化的基础词，指所加入的混合本身

senses.title: The process
senses.titleCN: 合金化：向金属中加入元素的工序
senses.definition: the deliberate addition of elements to a metal in order to change its properties
senses.definitionCN: 有意向金属中加入元素以改变其性能的做法
senses.example: Alloying raises the strength of aluminium without making it much heavier.
senses.exampleCN: 合金化提高了铝的强度，却没有让它重太多。
senses.why: The verb alloy means to combine metals; the -ing form names the ongoing technical operation, with the emphasis on the act of adding rather than on the resulting material.
senses.whyCN: 动词 alloy 意为把金属合在一起；动名词形式命名正在进行的技术作业，重点在「加入」这个动作，而不是所得的合金。

senses.title: One heat, one addition
senses.titleCN: 一次操作：某一炉的合金化作业
senses.definition: a single act of adding elements to a particular melt
senses.definitionCN: 对某一炉熔体进行的一次元素加入
senses.example: The alloying of this heat took twenty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 这一炉的合金化用了二十分钟。
senses.why: A countable use appears when the process is tied to one furnace charge, because each heat has its own timing and its own record.
senses.whyCN: 当过程与某一炉炉料绑定时，就会出现可数用法，因为每一炉都有自己的时间与记录。

senses.title: The element's role
senses.titleCN: 合金元素的作用：少量加入、明显改变
senses.definition: the function of an element added in small amounts to control a property
senses.definitionCN: 以少量加入、用来控制某项性能的元素所起的作用
senses.example: Chromium is the alloying element that makes stainless steel resist rust.
senses.exampleCN: 铬是那种让不锈钢抗锈的合金元素。
senses.why: A small addition can change a large property, so the added element is treated as an agent with a job rather than as a filler.
senses.whyCN: 少量加入就能改变很大的性能，因此被加入的元素被看作承担任务的角色，而不是填充物。

senses.title: How it works inside
senses.titleCN: 冶金机理：固溶、析出与晶粒控制
senses.definition: the mechanisms by which added elements enter the solid metal, such as solid solution, precipitation and grain refinement
senses.definitionCN: 加入的元素进入固态金属的机制，如固溶、析出与晶粒细化
senses.example: Solid-solution alloying distorts the lattice and blocks dislocation motion.
senses.exampleCN: 固溶合金化使晶格畸变，从而阻碍位错运动。
senses.why: An added atom does not disappear: it either fits into the lattice or forms its own particles, and either way it interferes with the movement that lets metals deform.
senses.whyCN: 加入的原子不会消失：它要么嵌进晶格，要么形成自己的颗粒；两种方式都会干扰金属变形所依赖的运动。

senses.title: Designing the recipe
senses.titleCN: 配比设计：成分与加入量的确定
senses.definition: choosing which elements to add and in what amounts for a target property
senses.definitionCN: 为达成某项目标性能而选择加入哪些元素、各加多少
senses.example: Alloying for marine service means balancing chromium against cost.
senses.exampleCN: 为海洋环境做合金化，意味着在铬含量与成本之间取平衡。
senses.why: Every addition buys one property and pays for it in another, so the craft becomes a trade-off rather than a simple strengthening step.
senses.whyCN: 每一种加入都换来一项性能，同时又在另一项上付出代价，因此这门手艺成了权衡，而不是简单的强化步骤。

senses.title: The property changed
senses.titleCN: 性能后果：强度、耐蚀与导电的变化
senses.definition: the resulting change in strength, hardness, corrosion resistance or conductivity
senses.definitionCN: 由此产生的强度、硬度、耐蚀性或导电性的变化
senses.example: Alloying improves corrosion resistance but lowers conductivity.
senses.exampleCN: 合金化提高耐蚀性，却降低了导电性。
senses.why: The point of the operation is a measurable difference, so the word often appears where results are compared rather than where metals are described.
senses.whyCN: 这道工序的目的就是一种可测量的差别，因此这个词常出现在比较结果的地方，而不是描述金属的地方。

senses.title: In the plant
senses.titleCN: 工业实践：炼钢与铝合金车间里的合金化
senses.definition: the industrial practice of alloying in steelmaking and light-metal plants
senses.definitionCN: 炼钢与轻金属工厂中实际的合金化作业
senses.example: Alloying is done in the ladle, just before the steel is cast.
senses.exampleCN: 合金化在钢包中进行，就在浇铸之前。
senses.why: Timing is part of the craft: adding an element too early lets it burn away, so the operation is placed at a precise point in the plant's sequence.
senses.whyCN: 时机本身就是手艺的一部分：加得太早元素会被烧掉，因此这道操作被安排在工厂流程中的一个精确位置。

senses.title: A metaphor of blending
senses.titleCN: 比喻：把不同成分融为一体的过程
senses.definition: a figurative process of combining different elements into one whole
senses.definitionCN: 比喻义：把不同成分融合成一个整体的过程
senses.example: The alloying of two traditions produced a style that belonged to neither.
senses.exampleCN: 两种传统的融合，产生了一种不属于任何一方的风格。
senses.why: When metals are alloyed, each loses its separate identity while changing the whole; the same image describes cultures, styles and ideas that merge.
senses.whyCN: 金属合金化时，各自失去独立身份却改变了整体；同一个意象可以描述融合的文化、风格与观念。

intro.en: Alloying is the verbal noun of alloy, a word whose root means 'to bind'. Its form is modern, but the operation it names is as old as the first deliberately mixed melt.
intro.cn: alloying 是 alloy 的动名词，而 alloy 的词根意为「绑」。它的形态是现代形成的，但它命名的操作，与人类第一次有意配制的熔体一样古老。

items.en: Alligare, from ad- 'to' and ligare 'to bind', meant to tie one thing to another. The derivation is generally accepted and explains both alloy and ally.
items.cn: alligare 由 ad-「向」与 ligare「绑」构成，意为把一物系到另一物上。这一派生是公认的，也同时解释了 alloy 与 ally。

items.en: Old French aloier applied the Latin verb to the combining of metals, and the noun aloi passed into English, where the verb alloy followed.
items.cn: 古法语 aloier 把这个拉丁动词用于金属的合并，名词 aloi 进入英语，动词 alloy 随后出现。

items.en: The noun is recorded in English from the sixteenth century and the verb a little later. The -ing form is the ordinary verbal noun that English builds from any verb.
items.cn: 名词自十六世纪见于英语，动词稍晚出现。动名词形式是英语从任何动词都能构成的常规名词。

items.en: The technical sense narrows to the deliberate addition of elements to a melt, as distinct from the simple mixing of scrap or the accidental contamination of a charge.
items.cn: 技术义收窄为有意向熔体中加入元素，以区别于废料的简单混合或炉料的意外污染。

items.en: Twentieth-century steelmaking and light-metal production turned alloying into a measured step with its own ladle timing, its own addition agents and its own quality records.
items.cn: 二十世纪的炼钢与轻金属生产，把合金化变成一个有计量、有钢包时机、有添加介质、有质量记录的工序。

items.en: Dating and usage: the earliest English dates are approximate, and the shift from 'binding' to 'adding an element' happened through trade usage rather than by any recorded decision.
items.cn: 年代与行业用法：最早的英语年代只是大致，而从「绑合」到「加入元素」的转变是经由行业用法发生的，并无任何有记录的约定。

note.en: Group one separates the close forms of the same family; group two separates alloying from other ways of changing a metal.
note.cn: 第一组把同族的近形形式分开；第二组把合金化与改变金属的其他方式分开。

entries.definition: The substance itself, or the verb of mixing; alloying names the ongoing operation.
entries.definitionCN: 物质本身，或混合的动词；alloying 命名正在进行的操作。

entries.definition: The state after the operation; alloying is the act, alloyed is the metal that has undergone it.
entries.definitionCN: 操作之后的状态；alloying 是动作，alloyed 是经历了该动作的金属。

entries.definition: The element added, not the process of adding it; the phrase names a role inside the operation.
entries.definitionCN: 被加入的元素，而不是加入它的过程；这个短语命名操作中的一个角色。

entries.definition: Steel that has been alloyed; it is the output of alloying, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 经过合金化的钢；它是合金化的产出，不是动作。

entries.definition: Alloying with very small amounts of an element, enough to change grain size but not composition class.
entries.definitionCN: 只加入极少量元素的合金化，足以改变晶粒尺寸却不改变材料类别。

entries.definition: Adding trace elements to a semiconductor to change its conductivity; the idea is similar but the field is not metallurgy.
entries.definitionCN: 向半导体加入微量元素以改变导电性；思路相似，但领域不是冶金。

entries.definition: Mixing materials without melting them together; alloying requires a melt so that the elements dissolve.
entries.definitionCN: 不把材料熔在一起地混合；合金化要求熔体，以便元素相互溶解。

entries.definition: A pre-made rich alloy added to a melt to introduce an element easily; it is a tool of alloying, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 预先配好的高含量合金，加入熔体以便容易地引入某种元素；它是合金化的工具，而不是过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the binding root, the real sequence in a plant, and the real trade-off words.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「绑」的词根、工厂里的真实顺序，以及真实的权衡词。

normal.en: The root is 'bind': alloying ties an extra element into the metal so that it cannot be separated by simple melting.
normal.cn: 词根是「绑」：合金化把额外元素绑进金属里，使其无法靠简单熔炼分开。

normal.en: The plant order is melt, alloy, cast: the addition happens in the ladle, just before the metal leaves it.
normal.cn: 工厂顺序是熔、合金化、浇铸：加入发生在钢包里，就在金属离开它之前。

normal.en: The typical gains and losses are a pair: more strength for less ductility, more corrosion resistance for less conductivity.
normal.cn: 典型的得失成对出现：强度换来延性损失，耐蚀换来导电下降。

normal.en: The family is regular: alloy for the material, alloyed for the result, alloying for the act, alloying element for the ingredient.
normal.cn: 同族形式很规整：合金指材料，已合金化的状态指结果，合金化指动作，加入的元素指成分。

normal.en: Chromium, nickel and molybdenum are the usual named additions in stainless and high-strength steels.
normal.cn: 铬、镍与钼是不锈钢与高强钢中最常被点名的添加元素。

abstract.en: Picture a single foreign atom sitting in a neat lattice, pushing its neighbours slightly out of line.
abstract.cn: 想象一个外来原子坐在整齐的晶格里，把邻近原子稍稍挤歪。

abstract.en: Picture a recipe where every ingredient you add takes away something else, so no dish is free.
abstract.cn: 想象一份配方，每加一味料就要拿走另一样东西，因此没有一道菜是白得的。

abstract.en: Picture two traditions melting into a third style that neither could have produced alone.
abstract.cn: 想象两种传统熔成第三种风格，而这种风格任何一方单独都做不出来。

examples.en: Alloying with a little chromium turns ordinary steel into stainless steel.
examples.cn: 加入少量铬的合金化，把普通钢变成不锈钢。

examples.en: The alloying step is recorded for every heat.
examples.cn: 每一炉都记录了合金化这一步。

examples.en: Microalloying saves cost by using grams rather than kilos of the added element.
examples.cn: 微合金化用克而不是公斤的加入量，从而节省成本。

dict_mnemonic.text: alloy（合金）+ ing（过程）＝ 合金化；记「炉前加料、成分改写、性能改变」。

root: alloy 来自拉丁 alligare「绑到……上」（ad- + ligare「绑」），经古法语进入英语；加 -ing 构成动名词，指有意向金属熔体加入元素的工序。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one addition: the process, one heat's operation, the added element's role, the mechanism inside, the recipe, the property changed, the plant practice, and a metaphor of merging.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着一次「加入」展开：工艺本身、某一炉的操作、加入元素的作用、内部机理、配比设计、性能变化、工厂实践，以及融合的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small bright lump is pushed into a churning melt, and the charge record is rewritten.
core.cn: 核心意象：一小块银亮金属被压进翻涌的熔体，炉料记录随之改写。

branches.en: THE OPERATION: the deliberate act of adding elements, named as a process.
branches.cn: 操作层：有意加入元素的行为，作为过程被命名。

branches.en: THE HEAT AND THE PLANT: one charge's timing, and the place in the works where the addition is made.
branches.cn: 炉次与工厂：某一炉的时机，以及工厂中进行加入的位置。

branches.en: THE INGREDIENT AND THE RECIPE: what is added, and how much of it is chosen.
branches.cn: 成分与配方：加入什么，以及加入多少。

branches.en: THE MECHANISM: the foreign atom enters the lattice or forms particles, and blocks deformation.
branches.cn: 机理层：外来原子进入晶格或形成颗粒，从而阻碍变形。

branches.en: THE RESULT AND THE METAPHOR: a measured property changes, and different traditions merge into one style.
branches.cn: 结果与比喻：可测量的性能发生变化，不同传统融合成一种风格。

intro.en: Alloying is a verb plus the ordinary -ing noun ending; its technical vocabulary is built by adding prefixes such as micro- and de-.
intro.cn: alloying 是动词加普通的 -ing 名词词尾；它的技术词汇靠 micro-、de- 这类前缀继续扩展。

latinIntro.en: The root is Latin alligare, from ligare 'to bind'; the same root reached English through ally, so the two words are relatives in origin but not in meaning.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是拉丁 alligare，出自 ligare「绑」；同一词根经 ally 进入英语，因此两词在来源上是亲属，在意义上不是。

definition_zh: 家长式统治；家长作风；父权主义
definition_en: the habit of deciding for others on the grounds that one knows what is good for them
core_image: 一位家长替全家做了所有决定，还坚持说这是为每个人好
scene: 公司给员工安排了宿舍、食堂和作息表，说是替他们省心。 The company provided housing, meals and a timetable for its workers, saying it was saving them trouble, a paternalism that came with a rent-free roof.
sceneCN: 这里 paternalism 指雇主的家长作风（第 1 个义项：雇主家长作风）；句意为公司给员工安排宿舍、食堂与作息表，说是替他们省心，这种家长作风还附赠一个免租房顶。

pos.zh: 家长式统治；家长作风；父权主义

senses.title: Employer paternalism
senses.definition: a firm that houses, feeds and supervises its workers as if they were children
senses.definitionCN: 像对待孩子一样给工人提供住处、饭食并加以监管的企业做法
senses.example: The mill's paternalism included a school and a chapel.
senses.exampleCN: 这家纺织厂的家长作风还包括一所学校和一座礼拜堂。
senses.why: Care and control arrive in the same van.
senses.whyCN: 照顾与控制是同一辆车送来的。

senses.title: State paternalism
senses.definition: a government that restricts choices because it claims to know better
senses.definitionCN: 以「更懂」为由限制选择空间的政府做法
senses.example: The smoking ban was defended as benevolent paternalism.
senses.exampleCN: 禁烟令被辩护为仁慈的家长式治理。
senses.why: The word names the trade: some freedom for some safety.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名那笔交易：用一些自由换一些安全。

senses.title: Colonial paternalism
senses.definition: rule that treats a colonised people as wards in need of guidance
senses.definitionCN: 把被殖民民族当作需要指导的受监护人的统治
senses.example: The district officer's paternalism infuriated the new assembly.
senses.exampleCN: 地区官员的家长作风激怒了新议会。
senses.why: Here the word exposes the insult inside the kindness.
senses.whyCN: 这里的词揭开了善意里藏着的轻蔑。

senses.title: Medical paternalism
senses.definition: the tradition of deciding for a patient rather than with him
senses.definitionCN: 替病人决定而不是与病人共同决定的传统
senses.example: Medical paternalism once kept diagnoses from the sick.
senses.exampleCN: 医疗父权主义曾把诊断瞒着病人。
senses.why: The profession's authority was once thought to need no consent.
senses.whyCN: 这个行业的权威曾被认为无需同意。

senses.title: Legal paternalism
senses.definition: laws that protect people by limiting what they may choose
senses.definitionCN: 以限制选择来保护人的法律思路
senses.example: Helmet laws rest on a legal paternalism few drivers accept.
senses.exampleCN: 头盔法建立在一种少有司机接受的家长主义上。
senses.why: The argument is about who owns a life: the person or the state.
senses.whyCN: 争论在于一条命归谁：本人，还是国家。

senses.title: Family paternalism
senses.definition: a father's assumption that his judgement settles the household's questions
senses.definitionCN: 父亲认为自己的判断就能定下家中问题的假定
senses.example: The family ran on a quiet paternalism no one dared name.
senses.exampleCN: 这个家靠一种无人敢点名的安静父权运转。
senses.why: The word begins at home and then expands to institutions.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从家里开始，然后扩展到机构。

senses.title: Condescending benevolence
senses.definition: the manner of helping someone while making his own judgement look small
senses.definitionCN: 一边帮忙一边让对方的判断显得微不足道的态度
senses.example: She resented the paternalism of being told to rest.
senses.exampleCN: 被人叫去休息时，她厌恶那种居高临下的善意。
senses.why: Kindness can be a way of taking the pen out of another hand.
senses.whyCN: 善意可以是把笔从别人手里拿走的一种方式。

senses.title: Critique of paternalism
senses.definition: the argument that people should be allowed to make their own mistakes
senses.definitionCN: 主张人应当被允许自己犯错的论证
senses.example: The essay attacked paternalism in the name of dignity.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章以尊严之名抨击家长主义。
senses.why: The word is most often used by its opponents, which is why it rarely sounds neutral.
senses.whyCN: 这个词多由反对者使用，所以它很少听起来中性。

intro.en: Paternalism is made from the Latin word for father: the ruler is imagined as a parent, and the ruled as children.
intro.cn: paternalism 由拉丁语的「父亲」造出：统治者被想象为家长，被统治者被想象为孩子。

items.en: Pater meant 'father', the root of paternal, patron and patrician.
items.cn: pater 意为「父亲」，是 paternal、patron 与 patrician 的词根。

items.en: Paternal meant 'of a father', as opposed to maternal, of a mother.
items.cn: paternal 意为「父亲的」，与 maternal（母亲的）相对。

items.en: Nineteenth-century writers used paternalism for employers who governed their workers' whole lives.
items.cn: 十九世纪作家用 paternalism 指管理工人全部生活的雇主。

items.en: Twentieth-century politics made it a term of argument about the welfare state.
items.cn: 二十世纪政治把它变成关于福利国家的争论术语。

items.en: Today it is applied to medicine, law, colonial rule and ordinary condescension.
items.cn: 今天它被用于医学、法律、殖民统治与日常的居高临下。

note.en: The look-alike group is the pater family; the near-meaning group separates patriarchy, condescension and authoritarianism.
note.cn: 形近组是 pater 词族；近义组把「父权制」「居高临下」与「威权主义」分开。

entries.definition: of a father.
entries.definitionCN: 父亲的。

entries.definition: one who governs like a father.
entries.definitionCN: 像家长一样治理的人。

entries.definition: acting like a father toward others.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人行家长作风的。

entries.definition: in a fatherly, controlling way.
entries.definitionCN: 以家长式控制的方式。

entries.definition: a social order ruled by fathers.
entries.definitionCN: 由父亲们统治的社会秩序。

entries.definition: treating others as inferior.
entries.definitionCN: 把他人当作低人一等。

entries.definition: rule that demands obedience.
entries.definitionCN: 要求服从的统治。

entries.definition: support given from above.
entries.definitionCN: 自上而下的庇护。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a parent who has already decided for everyone.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「家长已经替所有人做完决定」的画面。

normal.en: Paternalism holds pater, Latin for father; the state is cast as a parent.
normal.cn: paternalism 里藏着 pater（拉丁语的父亲）；国家被安排成家长角色。

normal.en: Think of a timetable pinned to the fridge for grown adults.
normal.cn: 想象一张钉在冰箱上、却给成年人看的作息表。

normal.en: Pa-ter-nal-ism: four beats, each one a decision made for you.
normal.cn: pa-ter-nal-ism：四拍，每一拍都是一个替你做的决定。

normal.en: Say puh-TUR-nuh-li-zum; the stress is on the father, not the system.
normal.cn: 读成 puh-TUR-nuh-li-zum，重音在父亲，不在制度。

normal.en: Pair it with consent: paternalism is care that forgot to ask.
normal.cn: 把它和 consent 配对：家长主义是忘了问一声的照顾。

abstract.en: Paternalism is not cruelty; it is kindness that has stopped listening.
abstract.cn: 家长主义不是残酷；它是停止了倾听的善意。

abstract.en: The test is simple: who gets to decide, and who is told afterwards.
abstract.cn: 检验很简单：谁来决定，谁事后被告知。

abstract.en: A welfare state and a mill town can share the same shape, one with forms and one with houses.
abstract.cn: 福利国家与纺织镇可以共享同一个形状，一个用表格，一个用宿舍。

examples.en: The company provided housing and a timetable, a paternalism that came with a roof.
examples.cn: 公司提供宿舍和作息表，这种家长作风还附赠一个房顶。

examples.en: The smoking ban was defended as benevolent paternalism.
examples.cn: 禁烟令被辩护为仁慈的家长式治理。

examples.en: She resented the paternalism of being told to rest.
examples.cn: 被人叫去休息时，她厌恶那种居高临下的善意。

dict_mnemonic.text: pater（父亲）+ nal + ism（主义）：像父亲一样替别人决定，就是「家长主义」。

root: 拉丁语 pater（父亲）加形容词词尾 -nal 与名词词尾 -ism

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all put one person in the parent's chair: an employer, a state, a colony, a doctor, a law, a father, a helper and a critic.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把一个人放上家长的位子：雇主、国家、殖民地、医生、法律、父亲、帮忙的人与批评者。

core.en: A PARENT WHO HAS ALREADY DECIDED
core.cn: 已经替所有人做完决定的家长

branches.en: A firm and a state acting as parent.
branches.cn: 像家长一样行事的公司与国家。

branches.en: A colony and a clinic, where authority is older than consent.
branches.cn: 权威早于同意的殖民地与诊所。

branches.en: A law that protects by limiting and a father who settles matters.
branches.cn: 以限制保护人的法律与替家中定事的父亲。

branches.en: Kindness delivered from above.
branches.cn: 从上面递下来的善意。

branches.en: The argument made against all of it.
branches.cn: 针对这一切提出的论证。

intro.en: The pater family is about fathers and patrons: paternal care, patronage, and a patriarchy that runs on the same root.
intro.cn: pater 词族关乎父亲与庇护者：paternal 的照顾、patronage 的庇护，以及同根运转的 patriarchy。

latinIntro.en: Latin pater supplies the father; the endings -nal and -ism turn him into a manner and then a system.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pater 提供父亲；词尾 -nal 与 -ism 先把他变成一种态度，再变成一套制度。

definition_zh: v. 攥紧（拳头）；咬紧（牙关）；紧紧握住
definition_en: to close your hand or teeth tightly, or hold something very firmly
core_image: 愤怒时拳头一寸寸收紧
scene: 她气得攥紧了拳头，一句话也没说。 She clenched her fists in anger and said nothing.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：clench 指攥紧拳头；句意是她气得攥紧了拳头，一句话也没说。

senses.title: To close the hand tightly
senses.definition: to curl the fingers into a hard fist
senses.definitionCN: 把手指紧紧握成硬拳
senses.example: She clenched her fists and stepped forward.
senses.exampleCN: 她攥紧拳头走上前。
senses.why: Old English clencan means to hold fast.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 clencan 意为抓紧。

senses.title: To set the teeth or jaw
senses.definition: to press the teeth together hard, often in pain or anger
senses.definitionCN: 常因疼痛或愤怒而用力咬合牙关
senses.example: He clenched his jaw and kept silent.
senses.exampleCN: 他咬紧牙关，一声不吭。
senses.why: The grip of the fist moved to the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 握拳的用力转移到了嘴上。

senses.title: To hold something firmly
senses.definition: to grip an object and refuse to let it go
senses.definitionCN: 抓住某物不肯松手
senses.example: She clenched the letter until it crumpled.
senses.exampleCN: 她把信攥得皱成一团。
senses.why: A closing hand also means a kept object.
senses.whyCN: 合拢的手也意味着抓住的东西。

intro.en: Clench is an old English verb of holding fast that moved from fists to jaws.
intro.cn: clench 是表示抓紧的古英语动词，从拳头延伸到牙关。

items.en: Clencan means to hold fast or clinch.
items.cn: clencan 意为紧握、扣紧。

items.en: Clenched appears as a past form of gripping.
items.cn: 中古英语 clenched 表示抓紧过的。

items.en: Writers describe clenched fists in anger.
items.cn: 十六世纪作家描写愤怒时握紧的拳头。

items.en: Clenched teeth become a set phrase for endurance.
items.cn: 十九世纪「咬紧牙关」成为忍受的固定说法。

items.en: The verb covers hands, teeth and gripped objects.
items.cn: 现代用法涵盖手、牙与紧握之物。

note.en: The look-alike group is a near spelling; the near-meaning group names other kinds of tight holding.
note.cn: 形近组是相近拼写；近义组列出其他紧握的说法。

entries.definition: To settle a deal or grapple close.
entries.definitionCN: 敲定；扭打。

entries.definition: To hold something tightly.
entries.definitionCN: 紧抓。

entries.definition: A hook that holds two parts together.
entries.definitionCN: 扣住两部分的钩扣。

entries.definition: To hold something firmly.
entries.definitionCN: 紧握。

entries.definition: To take hold of something.
entries.definitionCN: 抓住。

entries.definition: To make something tighter.
entries.definitionCN: 收紧。

normalIntro.en: A clenched hand is a lock made of fingers.
normalIntro.cn: 攥紧的手就是用手指做成的锁。

normal.en: Clench sounds like a latch snapping shut.
normal.cn: clench 听起来像门闩咔地扣上。

normal.en: Fingers curl into a fist.
normal.cn: 手指蜷成拳头。

normal.en: Teeth clench in pain.
normal.cn: 疼痛时咬紧牙。

normal.en: A hand can clench a letter.
normal.cn: 手能把信攥紧。

normal.en: Clinch is the close cousin.

abstract.en: Anger given a shape.
abstract.cn: 被赋予形状的愤怒。

abstract.en: A hand saying no.
abstract.cn: 一只说「不」的手。

abstract.en: Strength pressed into a small space.
abstract.cn: 压在狭小空间里的力量。

examples.en: He clenched his fist behind his back.
examples.cn: 他在背后握紧了拳头。

examples.en: The patient clenched her teeth against the pain.
examples.cn: 病人咬紧牙关忍痛。

examples.en: She clenched the railing as the bus turned.
examples.cn: 公交车转弯时她紧紧抓住扶手。

dict_mnemonic.text: clench 的读音像关节「咔」地收紧：拳、牙、手一起用力。

root: 古英语 clencan（抓紧、扣紧）→ 中古英语 clenchen → 现代 clench

sensesIntro.en: One verb of shutting covers a fist, a jaw and a gripped object.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「合紧」动词涵盖拳头、牙关与紧握之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: knuckles whitening in a closed fist
core.cn: 核心意象：握紧的拳头指节发白

branches.en: A fist raised at a protest.
branches.cn: 抗议中举起的拳头。

branches.en: A jaw locked in pain.
branches.cn: 因疼痛咬紧的下颌。

branches.en: A letter crushed in a hand.
branches.cn: 被手攥皱的信。

branches.en: Fingers round a bus railing.
branches.cn: 抓着公交扶手的手指。

branches.en: Tension held in hand and mouth.
branches.cn: 握在手与嘴里的紧张。

tenere 产生 tense 与 tenant。

definition_zh: 民间世代口耳相传的故事、歌谣、信仰与习俗的总称
definition_en: the traditional stories, songs, beliefs and customs of a community, passed on by word of mouth
core_image: 村口的老槐树下，几个孩子围着一位老人，听他讲一个没有书的故事
scene: 村口的老槐树下，几个孩子围着一位老人，听他讲一个没有书的故事。 The folklore of the valley survives mainly in songs sung at harvest.
sceneCN: 这里 folklore 指「民间口耳相传的故事与习俗之总称」（第 1 个义项：一个社群传下来的口头传统）；句意为这个山谷的民间文化主要靠丰收时唱的歌流传。可辨识物件：老槐树、老人、孩子、歌谱。

senses.title: A community's oral inheritance
senses.titleCN: 社群口耳相传的文化遗产
senses.definition: the body of stories, songs and customs that a community passes on without writing them down
senses.definitionCN: 一个社群在不依靠书写的情况下传递的故事、歌谣与习俗整体
senses.example: The folklore of the valley survives mainly in songs sung at harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷的民间文化主要靠丰收时唱的歌流传。
senses.why: folk names the people and lore names what they teach, so the compound is learning that lives in a community rather than a library.
senses.whyCN: folk 指民众，lore 指他们所教的东西，因此这个复合词指活在社群中而非图书馆里的学问。

senses.title: Traditional tales and legends
senses.definition: narrative folklore such as fairy tales, ghost stories and local legends
senses.definitionCN: 如童话、鬼故事与地方传说这类叙事性民俗
senses.example: Every village tells a folklore tale about the old bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 每个村庄都有一则关于那座旧桥的民间故事。
senses.why: stories are the part of folklore that travels furthest without being written.
senses.whyCN: 故事是民俗中最能在不书写的情况下远行传播的部分。

senses.title: Songs and ballads
senses.definition: sung folklore, including work songs, laments and ballads
senses.definitionCN: 歌唱形态的民俗，包括劳动号子、挽歌与叙事歌谣
senses.example: The folklore of the fishing villages is carried by work songs.
senses.exampleCN: 渔村的民间文化由劳动号子承载。
senses.why: melody is a memory aid, so song is the oldest archive of the unschooled.
senses.whyCN: 旋律是记忆的助手，因此歌谣是未受教育者最古老的档案。

senses.title: Popular beliefs and superstitions
senses.definition: unwritten beliefs about luck, spirits, omens and protective practices
senses.definitionCN: 关于运气、鬼魂、预兆与护身做法的成文之外的信念
senses.example: Folklore about the crossroads kept travellers from walking at night.
senses.exampleCN: 关于十字路口的民间说法让旅人不敢夜行。
senses.why: beliefs explain misfortune cheaply, and folklore stores them where no doctrine reaches.
senses.whyCN: 信念能廉价地解释不幸，而民俗把它们储存在教义触及不到之处。

senses.title: Craft and material folk culture
senses.definition: traditional making of tools, cloth, food and dwellings
senses.definitionCN: 工具、织物、食物与居所的传统制作方式
senses.example: The museum collects folklore in the form of baskets and looms.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆以篮子与织机的形式收藏民间工艺。
senses.why: lore is not only told but made, and objects carry instruction in their shape.
senses.whyCN: 学问不只靠讲述，也靠制作，器物在形状里携带技艺。

senses.title: The object of a scholarly discipline
senses.definition: the material that folklorists collect, classify and interpret
senses.definitionCN: 民俗学者采集、分类与解释的材料
senses.example: The journal treats folklore as evidence, not as quaint decoration.
senses.exampleCN: 该期刊把民俗当作证据，而非古雅的装饰。
senses.why: once a field has a name for its material, the material becomes an object of study.
senses.whyCN: 当一个领域为自己的材料命名，这些材料就成了研究对象。

senses.title: The oral tradition of one group
senses.definition: the specific verbal inheritance of a people, region or occupation
senses.definitionCN: 某个民族、地区或职业特有的口头遗产
senses.example: Miners kept their own folklore of underground spirits.
senses.exampleCN: 矿工有自己的地下神灵传说。
senses.why: occupations form their own risk-sharing culture with its own stories.
senses.whyCN: 职业会形成自己的风险分担文化，也有自己的故事。

senses.title: Folk creation in the internet age
senses.definition: jokes, memes and stories that spread anonymously online in the old folk manner
senses.definitionCN: 以古老民间方式在网上匿名传播的笑话、模因与故事
senses.example: Researchers now study the folklore of message boards.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者如今研究论坛上的民间创作。
senses.why: the medium changed, but anonymous communal retelling is the same act as before.
senses.whyCN: 媒介变了，但匿名集体复述仍是同一种行为。

senses.title: A story dismissed as untrue
senses.titleCN: 被当作「传说」的不实说法
senses.definition: used dismissively of a claim that people repeat without evidence
senses.definitionCN: 轻蔑地指人们无证据却反复传播的说法
senses.example: The idea that the tower has no foundations is pure folklore.
senses.exampleCN: 说那座塔没有地基纯粹是民间传说。
senses.why: when a repeated story is doubted, folklore becomes a word for unverified belief.
senses.whyCN: 当反复流传的故事受到怀疑，folklore 就变成「未经证实的说法」之词。

intro.en: Folklore is a deliberately coined English compound: folk, from Old English folc 'people', plus lore, from Old English lār 'teaching, learning'. It was proposed in 1846. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: folklore 是一个有意造出的英语复合词：folk 来自古英语 folc「民众」，lore 来自古英语 lār「教导、学问」。这个词于 1846 年被提出。年代均为约数。

items.en: Folc meant 'people, crowd, tribe'. The pre-Germanic shape is reconstructed, so the earlier form is not witnessed in any text.
items.cn: folc 意为「民众、人群、部族」。日耳曼语之前的形态属重构形式，更早的词形没有任何文本书证。

items.en: Lār meant 'teaching, instruction, learning', and still survives in lore and in learned.
items.cn: lār 意为「教导、传授、学问」，仍存于 lore 与 learned 之中。

items.en: In 1846 William Thoms proposed folklore to replace 'popular antiquities', and the word spread quickly through learned journals.
items.cn: 1846 年威廉·汤姆斯提出用 folklore 取代「民间古物」一词，这个词很快在学术刊物中传播。

items.en: It first meant the whole inherited culture of ordinary people, then narrowed to stories, songs and beliefs, then widened again to include craft and online creation.
items.cn: 它先指普通民众继承的整体文化，后收窄到故事、歌谣与信念，再扩展到工艺与网络创作。

items.en: The word now also serves as a mild dismissal of a claim that circulates without evidence.
items.cn: 如今这个词也用来轻微否定一种无证据却流传的说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Germanic origin): the older Germanic shape of folc is a reconstruction, and the pre-Germanic source of lār is not established.
items.cn: 来源不确定（日耳曼语之前的来源）：folc 更早的日耳曼语形态属重构形式；lār 在日耳曼语之前的来源无定论。

note.en: Group one holds forms built from the two halves of the compound; group two holds narrative or traditional genres often mistaken for it.
note.cn: 第一组是由复合词两半构成的词；第二组是常被与之混淆的叙事或传统类别。

entries.definition: Ordinary people or a particular people; folklore is what they pass on.
entries.definitionCN: 指普通民众或某一民族；folklore 是他们传下的东西。

entries.definition: Traditional knowledge on a subject, as in plant lore or seafaring lore.
entries.definitionCN: 指某一方面的传统知识，如植物知识或航海知识。

entries.definition: A person who collects and studies folklore; the suffix -ist names the person, not the material.
entries.definitionCN: 指采集与研究民俗的人；后缀 -ist 指人，而非材料。

entries.definition: Means 'of folklore', often used of art that borrows folk material.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「民间文化的」，常用于借用民间素材的艺术。

entries.definition: A story about a person or place, told as if historical; folklore is the whole field that contains it.
entries.definitionCN: 指关于某人或某地、仿佛历史般讲述的故事；folklore 是包含它的整个领域。

entries.definition: A story about gods or origins, usually tied to belief; folklore can be secular and everyday.
entries.definitionCN: 指关于神祇或起源的故事，通常与信仰相连；folklore 可以是世俗日常的。

entries.definition: Anything passed between generations, including law and craft; folklore stresses oral and communal forms.
entries.definitionCN: 指代代相传的一切，包括法律与技艺；folklore 强调口头与集体形式。

entries.definition: Recorded personal memories of events; folklore is communal and often older than any witness.
entries.definitionCN: 指记录下来的个人事件记忆；folklore 是集体的，往往比任何见证者更古老。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: folk 'people' plus lore 'teaching' gives 'the teaching of the people'.
normal.cn: folk「民众」加 lore「教导」，得「民众的学问」。

normal.en: The word was coined in 1846 to replace the phrase popular antiquities.
normal.cn: 这个词于 1846 年造出，用来取代「民间古物」这一说法。

normal.en: The family runs folk, lore, folklore, folkloric, folklorist and folkloristics.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 folk、lore、folklore、folkloric、folklorist 与 folkloristics。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: local folklore, rural folklore, folklore collector, folklore and myth.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：地方民俗、乡村民俗、民俗采集者、民俗与神话。

normal.en: The same word now covers memes and message-board stories, because the spread is still anonymous and communal.
normal.cn: 这个词如今也涵盖模因与论坛故事，因为传播仍是匿名且集体的。

abstract.en: Picture a library with no shelves, only voices.
abstract.cn: 想象一座没有书架、只有声音的图书馆。

abstract.en: Picture a story that changes a little each time it is told, and survives by changing.
abstract.cn: 想象一个故事每讲一次就变一点，并靠变化而存活。

abstract.en: Picture a path kept open by the people who retell it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条因不断被复述而保持畅通的路。

examples.en: She collected folklore from fishermen along the whole coast.
examples.cn: 她沿着整条海岸采集渔民的民间故事。

examples.en: The film borrows folklore but invents its own ending.
examples.cn: 这部电影借用了民间传说，却自编了结局。

examples.en: Online folklore spreads faster than any village tale.
examples.cn: 网络民间创作传播得比任何村中故事都快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「folk（民众）+ lore（学问）」——老百姓口口相传的学问

root: 古英语 folc「民众」+ 古英语 lār「教导、学问」；1846 年由威廉·汤姆斯造出，取代「民间古物」。日耳曼语之前的形态均属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one channel: knowledge is passed mouth to ear, and that channel then carries tales, songs, beliefs, craft, a discipline's evidence, one group's tradition, online creation and finally an unverified claim.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一条渠道展开：知识从口传到耳，这条渠道再依次承载故事、歌谣、信念、工艺、学科证据、某群体的传统、网络创作，最后承载未经证实的说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a library with no shelves, only voices passing a story hand to hand without paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座没有书架、只有声音的图书馆，故事不用纸便一手手传下去。

branches.en: THE CHANNEL AND ONE GROUP: the general inheritance, and the specific version kept by a people or trade.
branches.cn: 渠道与某一群体：普遍的继承，以及某个民族或行业保有的特定版本。

branches.en: STORIES: narrative is the part of the inheritance that travels furthest.
branches.cn: 故事：叙事是这份遗产中传播最远的部分。

branches.en: SONGS: melody carries what writing cannot reach.
branches.cn: 歌谣：旋律携带书写触及不到的东西。

branches.en: BELIEF AND OBJECT: superstition explains misfortune, and craft teaches through shape.
branches.cn: 信念与器物：迷信解释不幸，工艺通过形状传授技艺。

branches.en: EVIDENCE, NEW MEDIA, DOUBT: the material becomes a science, then a meme, and finally a word for what cannot be proved.
branches.cn: 证据、新媒介与怀疑：材料先成为科学，再成为模因，最后成为「无法证明之物」的说法。

intro.en: Folklore is a modern compound of two Old English words, so its parts are transparent and its family is built with English suffixes.
intro.cn: folklore 是两个古英语词构成的现代复合词，其成分清晰，词族由英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: No Latin borrowing stands behind this word; both halves are Old English, so no Latin source forms are recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后没有拉丁借词；两半都来自古英语，因此不列拉丁语源形式。

items.example: Folc is the ancestor of folk.
items.exampleCN: folc 是 folk 的祖先形式。

items.example: Lār survives in lore and in learned.
items.exampleCN: lār 存于 lore 与 learned 中。

items.example: Folk can also be an adjective, as in folk music.
items.exampleCN: folk 也可作形容词，如民间音乐。

items.example: Lore often appears in compounds such as plant lore.
items.exampleCN: lore 常出现在植物知识这类复合词中。

items.example: The compound replaced an older phrase.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词取代了更早的说法。
folkloric 意为与民俗有关的。

items.example: Folklorist names a collector or scholar.

items.meaning: deliberately plain and rural in style
items.example: Folksy is often a criticism of manufactured simplicity.
items.exampleCN: folksy 常批评人为制造的朴素。

items.meaning: the customary ways of a people
items.example: Folkways are everyday custom rather than formal law.
items.exampleCN: folkways 指日常习俗，而非正式法律。

definition_zh: n. 不一致；不和谐；不协调
definition_en: a lack of agreement or harmony between people, things or sounds
core_image: 合唱团里一个人唱跑了调，指挥的手停在半空；齿轮组里有一个齿对不上，整台机器卡住
scene: 色彩之间的不协调让房间显得杂乱。 The disharmony of the colours made the room feel messy.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：颜色彼此不搭，整个房间显得杂乱。

senses.title: Lack of agreement between people
senses.definition: a lack of agreement or friendly feeling between people or groups
senses.definitionCN: （名词）人或群体之间缺乏一致或友好感情
senses.example: Disharmony between the two groups slowed the work.
senses.exampleCN: 两个群体之间的不和拖慢了工作。
senses.why: A conductor with a hand frozen while one singer is off key.
senses.whyCN: 指挥的手停在半空，因为有一个歌手唱跑了调。

senses.title: Things that do not fit
senses.definition: a failure of parts, colours or elements to fit together well
senses.definitionCN: （名词）部件、颜色或元素彼此搭配不好
senses.example: The disharmony of the colours made the room feel messy.
senses.exampleCN: 色彩之间的不协调让房间显得杂乱。
senses.why: A gear whose teeth will not meet the next wheel.
senses.whyCN: 一个齿轮的齿咬不上旁边的轮子。

senses.title: Sounds that clash
senses.definition: a lack of harmony in music or sound
senses.definitionCN: （名词）音乐或声音中缺乏和谐
senses.example: The disharmony in the final chord was deliberate.
senses.exampleCN: 最后那个和弦的不和谐是刻意为之。
senses.why: Two strings tuned a little apart on one guitar.
senses.whyCN: 同一把吉他上两根音调得略微错开的弦。

intro.en: Disharmony is dis- plus harmony; harmony comes from Greek harmonia, a fitting together, from harmos, a joint, so disharmony means joints that do not meet.
intro.cn: disharmony 由 dis-（否定）加 harmony（和谐）构成；harmony 来自希腊语 harmonia「接合在一起」，来自 harmos「接缝」，所以 disharmony 就是接缝对不上。

items.en: Greek harmos means a joint or fitting.
items.cn: 希腊语 harmos 意为接缝、接合。

items.en: Harmonia meant a fitting together, then agreement.
items.cn: harmonia 意为接合在一起，后来指一致。

items.en: Latin harmonia carried the musical sense of concord.
items.cn: 拉丁语 harmonia 带有音乐上协和的意思。

items.en: Old French harmonie entered for agreement of parts.
items.cn: 古法语 harmonie 表示各部分的一致。

items.en: Middle English armony became harmony.
items.cn: 中古英语 armony 变成 harmony。

items.en: Dis- gave disharmony, a lack of harmony.
items.cn: dis- 造出 disharmony，意为缺乏和谐。

note.en: Disharmony is harmony with the joints apart; its neighbours share the joint root or name a clash.
note.cn: disharmony 是接缝分开的 harmony；它的邻居要么同「接合」词根，要么指冲突。

entries.definition: agreement of parts, or pleasing combined sounds
entries.definitionCN: 各部分的一致，或悦耳的组合音

entries.definition: fitting together well; friendly and agreeing
entries.definitionCN: 搭配得当的；友好而一致的

entries.definition: not fitting together; lacking harmony
entries.definitionCN: 搭配不上的；缺乏和谐的

entries.definition: disagreement between people, or harsh combined sounds
entries.definitionCN: 人际不和，或刺耳的组合音

entries.definition: a serious disagreement or struggle between aims
entries.definitionCN: 目标之间严重的分歧或争斗

entries.definition: a situation where parts are not equal or balanced
entries.definitionCN: 各部分不相等或不平衡的状况

normalIntro.en: Five pictures of joints that will not meet.
normalIntro.cn: 五个接缝对不上的画面。

normal.cn: 指挥的手停在半空，因为有一个歌手唱跑了调。

normal.en: A red cushion dropped onto a pale green sofa.
normal.cn: 一个红靠垫扔在浅绿沙发上。

normal.en: Two puzzle pieces pressed together that refuse to join.
normal.cn: 两块按在一起却拼不上的拼图。

abstract.cn: 指挥的手停在半空，因为有一个歌手唱跑了调。

abstract.en: A gear whose teeth will not meet the next wheel.

examples.en: Disharmony in the team delayed the launch.
examples.cn: 团队内部的不协调推迟了发布。

examples.en: The disharmony of the two styles is obvious.
examples.cn: 两种风格之间的不协调显而易见。

examples.en: He played the chord to show disharmony.
examples.cn: 他弹那个和弦是为了展示不和谐。

dict_mnemonic.text: disharmony ＝ dis-（否定）＋ harmony（和谐，希腊语 harmonia「接合」，来自 harmos「接缝」）＝接缝对不上，「不和谐、不一致」；同根还有 harmonious（和谐的）、harmonize（使协调）。

root: 希腊语 harmos（接缝）→ harmonia（接合、一致）→ 拉丁语 harmonia → 古法语 harmonie → 英语 harmony → 加 dis- 成 disharmony

sensesIntro.en: Joints that will not meet: an off key singer, a gear that will not mesh and two strings tuned apart.
sensesIntro.cn: 对不上的接缝：跑调的歌手、咬合不上的齿轮与两根调错的弦。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gear whose teeth will not meet the next wheel while the hand of a conductor freezes in the air
core.cn: 核心意象：一个齿轮的齿咬不上旁边的轮子，同时指挥的手停在半空

branches.en: Two groups whose aims will not join.
branches.cn: 目标接不上的两个群体。
