branches.cn: 两者都是本该契合却契合不上的部分。

branches.en: Both produce a clash you can sense at once.
branches.cn: 两者都产生立刻能感到的冲突。

intro.en: Disharmony is dis- plus harmony; the joint root also builds harmonious, harmonize and harmony itself.
intro.cn: disharmony 由 dis- 加 harmony 构成；接合这个词根也造出 harmonious、harmonize 与 harmony 本身。

latinIntro.en: Greek harmos means a joint, harmonia a fitting together, and Latin libra a balance.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 harmos 意为接缝，harmonia 意为接合，拉丁语 libra 意为天平。

definition_zh: 繁殖；育种；饲养；教养；繁殖季
definition_en: the process of producing offspring, or the controlled improvement of animals and plants
core_image: 春天的鱼塘里，工人忙着分池、配对、记录鱼卵
scene: 鱼塘在春天进入最忙的季节，工人忙着分池和配对。场长说： Breeding starts when the water warms above fifteen degrees.
sceneCN: 这里指「繁殖」（第 1 个义项：生物产生后代的过程）；句意为当水温升到十五度以上时，繁殖就开始了。

pos.zh: 繁殖；育种；饲养；教养；繁殖季（不可数）

senses.title: The production of offspring
senses.definition: the process by which animals or plants produce young
senses.definitionCN: 动物或植物产生后代的过程
senses.example: Breeding starts when the water warms above fifteen degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 当水温升到十五度以上时，繁殖就开始了。
senses.why: The core sense is biological: one generation produces the next, with or without human help.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是生物的：一个世代产生下一个世代，无论有没有人帮助。

senses.title: Controlled breeding and improvement
senses.definition: the deliberate selection of parents to improve a line or breed
senses.definitionCN: 有意选择亲本以改良品系或品种
senses.example: Selective breeding raised the sugar content of the beets.
senses.exampleCN: 选择育种提高了甜菜的含糖量。
senses.why: Humans take the natural process and steer it, so breeding becomes a planned method of improvement.
senses.whyCN: 人类接手自然过程并操控方向，于是繁殖成为有计划的改良方法。

senses.title: Keeping and raising animals
senses.definition: the work of keeping animals for reproduction or production
senses.definitionCN: 为繁殖或生产而饲养动物的工作
senses.example: Fish breeding requires clean water and steady temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 鱼类养殖需要清洁的水与稳定的温度。
senses.why: Once animals are kept, breeding names the whole husbandry activity, not only the mating.
senses.whyCN: 一旦动物被饲养，breeding 就命名整套养殖活动，而不只是交配。

senses.title: Good manners or upbringing
senses.definition: the manners and behaviour produced by upbringing
senses.definitionCN: 由养育形成的举止与行为方式
senses.example: His calm breeding showed in every room he entered.
senses.exampleCN: 他从容的教养在每走进一个房间时都显露出来。
senses.why: The old metaphor treats upbringing as cultivation: a person is 'bred' the way an animal is bred.
senses.whyCN: 旧的隐喻把养育当作栽培：人像动物一样被「育」出来。

senses.title: The breeding season or behaviour
senses.definition: the period or set of behaviours associated with mating
senses.definitionCN: 与交配相关的时期或行为组合
senses.example: The birds return to the island for breeding in April.
senses.exampleCN: 这些鸟在四月回到岛上繁殖。
senses.why: Animals breed in seasons, so the noun also names the time and the behaviour that go with reproduction.
senses.whyCN: 动物在特定季节繁殖，因此这个名词也命名与繁殖相伴的时期与行为。

senses.title: Developing a new variety
senses.definition: the long process of producing a stable new variety
senses.definitionCN: 培育稳定新品种的长期过程
senses.example: The breeding of this rose took twelve years.
senses.exampleCN: 培育这个月季品种花了十二年。
senses.why: A variety is not made in one cross; breeding names the repeated cycles that stabilize it.
senses.whyCN: 一个品种不是一次杂交就能做成；breeding 命名使它稳定的反复循环。

senses.title: Mating arrangements
senses.definition: the pairing of selected males and females
senses.definitionCN: 把选定的雌雄个体配对
senses.example: The breeding of the two prize animals was arranged months ahead.
senses.exampleCN: 两头获奖动物的配种提前几个月就安排好了。
senses.why: In practice breeding often means the specific pairing decisions a manager makes.
senses.whyCN: 在实践中，breeding 常指管理者做出的具体配对决定。

senses.title: A place or source that fosters something
senses.definition: a situation or place that encourages something to develop
senses.definitionCN: 促使某事物发展的情境或场所
senses.example: Stagnant water is a breeding ground for mosquitoes.
senses.exampleCN: 积水是蚊子的滋生地。
senses.why: The picture of animals multiplying in a favorable place extends to anything that lets a problem multiply.
senses.whyCN: 动物在有利场所大量繁殖的图像，被扩展到任何让问题滋生的地方。

intro.en: Breeding is the noun from breed, which comes from Old English bredan 'to warm, cherish, produce young'. The word is native Germanic, with no Latin source. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: breeding 是 breed 的名词形式，而 breed 来自古英语 bredan「保暖、抚育、生育」。这个词是本族日耳曼词，没有拉丁语来源。年代均为约数。

items.en: Bredan meant 'to warm, keep warm, cherish', especially young. The sense 'produce offspring' grew from the care given to young animals.
items.cn: bredan 意为「保暖、保温、抚育」，尤指抚育幼仔。「生育后代」义从对幼仔的照料发展而来。

items.en: Breed is related to brood 'a family of young' and broth 'liquid in which food is cooked', both going back to a Germanic root connected with warming.
items.cn: breed 与 brood「一窝幼仔」、broth「煮食物的汤液」相关，它们都追溯到与「加温」有关的日耳曼词根。

items.en: In Middle English the verb extended from cherishing the young to producing them, and the noun breeding named the whole process.
items.cn: 在中古英语中，这个动词从抚育幼仔扩展到生育幼仔，名词 breeding 则命名整个过程。

items.en: By the sixteenth century breeding also meant the manners formed by upbringing, a metaphor of cultivation applied to people.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪，breeding 也指由养育形成的举止，这是把栽培隐喻用于人。

items.en: The nineteenth century made breeding a technical term for controlled improvement of plants and stock, alongside pedigree records and selection.
items.cn: 19 世纪使 breeding 成为有控改良动植物品种的技术术语，并与谱系记录和选择相伴。

items.en: Source uncertain (root): the deeper Indo-European origin of the Germanic warming root is reconstructed with competing accounts, and the first use of breeding for manners is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根）：日耳曼「加温」词根的更深印欧来源属重构，存在不同假说；breeding 表示举止的最早使用也只有大致年代。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same breed family that are easily confused; group two holds near terms for producing and raising young.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 breed 词族、容易混淆的形式；第二组是表示生育与养育的邻近词。

entries.definition: To produce offspring, or a group of animals of one type; breeding is the process noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指生育后代，或指一类动物；breeding 是过程名词。

entries.definition: The past tense and past participle of breed; it is a verb form, not the activity.
entries.definitionCN: breed 的过去式与过去分词；是动词形式，不是活动本身。

entries.definition: A person who breeds animals or plants; the -er suffix names the agent.
entries.definitionCN: 指从事动植物繁育的人；-er 后缀命名施动者。

entries.definition: The young of one hatching or birth, or to sit on eggs; it is related to breed but names the group or the sitting.
entries.definitionCN: 指一次孵化或生产的一窝幼仔，或指孵蛋；与 breed 相关，但命名群体或孵卧行为。

entries.definition: The biological process by which organisms make new organisms; it is wider and includes plants and microbes.
entries.definitionCN: 指生物产生新个体的生物学过程；范围更广，包括植物与微生物。

entries.definition: The care and feeding of young until they are independent; breeding is conception and birth, rearing comes after.
entries.definitionCN: 指对幼体的照料与喂养直到独立；breeding 关乎受孕与出生，rearing 在其后。

entries.definition: Producing new plants or spreading a group; it is common in horticulture and can be asexual.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生新植物或扩大群体；常用于园艺，也可以是无性的。

entries.definition: Preparing land and growing crops; it is about tending plants, not producing offspring.
entries.definitionCN: 指整地并种植作物；关乎照料植物，而非产生后代。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: breed + -ing: the process of producing young.
normal.cn: breed + -ing：产生后代的过程。

normal.en: The family runs breed, bred, breeder, breeding, crossbreeding, inbreeding.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 breed、bred、breeder、breeding、crossbreeding、inbreeding。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: breeding season, breeding program, captive breeding.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：繁殖季、育种计划、圈养繁殖。

normal.en: Selective breeding is the human-guided version of natural reproduction.
normal.cn: 选择育种是自然繁殖的人为指导版本。

normal.en: The figurative breeding ground lets a problem multiply like animals.
normal.cn: 比喻的滋生地让问题像动物一样大量繁殖。

abstract.en: Picture a pond in spring full of eggs and tiny fish.
abstract.cn: 想象春天的池塘满是鱼卵与小鱼。

abstract.en: Picture a gardener choosing which plants to let seed.
abstract.cn: 想象园丁挑选让哪些植物结籽。

abstract.en: Picture a person whose calm manners were formed at home.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人从容的举止是在家里养成的。

examples.en: Captive breeding saved the species from extinction.
examples.cn: 圈养繁殖把该物种从灭绝中救了回来。

examples.en: The breeding program selects for drought tolerance.
examples.cn: 这个育种计划选择耐旱性。

examples.en: The marsh is a breeding ground for thousands of birds.
examples.cn: 这片沼泽是成千上万只鸟的繁殖地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「布里丁」——春天里忙着配对、下仔、育幼的那段事 → 繁殖、育种

root: breed（古英语 bredan「保暖、抚育、生育」）+ -ing；本族日耳曼词，与 brood「一窝幼仔」、broth「汤液」相关，无拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one process: animals produce young, humans guide the process, and the same word extends to husbandry, manners, seasons and places where things multiply.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个过程展开：动物产生后代，人类引导这个过程，同一个词再延伸到养殖、举止、季节以及事物大量滋生的地方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spring pond busy with eggs, fry and caretakers.
core.cn: 核心意象：春天的池塘里满是鱼卵、小鱼与忙碌的照料者。

branches.en: BIOLOGY AND SEASON: producing young, and the time and behaviour that surround it.
branches.cn: 生物学与季节：产生后代，以及围绕它的时期与行为。

branches.en: HUMAN GUIDANCE: selection, long variety development and specific pairing decisions.
branches.cn: 人类引导：选择、长期的品种培育，以及具体配对决定。

branches.en: HUSBANDRY: keeping and raising animals becomes an occupation.
branches.cn: 养殖：饲养与养育动物成为一种职业。

branches.en: UPBRINGING: cultivation as a metaphor for manners.
branches.cn: 教养：把栽培用作举止的隐喻。

branches.en: METAPHOR: a place where something multiplies.
branches.cn: 比喻：某事物大量滋生的地方。

intro.en: Breeding is breed plus -ing. Both elements are native English, so the word has no Latin affix, though it belongs to the same Germanic family as brood.
intro.cn: breeding 是 breed 加 -ing。两个成分都是英语本族成分，因此这个词没有拉丁词缀，但它与 brood 同属日耳曼词族。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in breeding: breed comes from Old English bredan, and -ing is a native suffix. Latin has no share in this word.
latinIntro.cn: breeding 中没有拉丁成分：breed 来自古英语 bredan，-ing 是本族后缀。拉丁语与这个词无关。

items.structure: Old English bredan (to warm, cherish, produce young)
items.example: The rabbits breed twice a year.
items.exampleCN: 这些兔子一年繁殖两次。

items.example: The birds were bred in captivity.
items.exampleCN: 这些鸟在圈养环境中繁育。

items.meaning: a place where animals breed or problems multiply
items.meaningCN: 动物繁殖或问题滋生的地方
items.example: Warm shallow water is a breeding ground.
items.exampleCN: 温暖的浅水是一处繁殖地。

definition_zh: 社会学的；从社会结构角度解释的
definition_en: relating to sociology, or explaining behaviour by social structures rather than individual choices
core_image: 把一间屋子的墙拆掉，露出与整条街相连的水管
scene: 一份关于通勤时间的报告不再归咎于个人选择，而是追问住房与地铁线路的布局。 The report offers a sociological explanation of lateness.
sceneCN: 这里 sociological 指「从社会结构出发来解释的」（第 2 个义项：以社会结构而非个人来解释）；句意为这份报告对迟到给出了社会学解释。场景要素：通勤路线图、住房分布、报告封面。

pos.zh: 社会学的；从社会角度解释的

derivatives.zh: 由 sociological 去掉形容词后缀构成的名词，指社会学
由 sociological 加副词后缀构成，指从社会学角度
由 sociology 加表人后缀构成，指社会学者
与 sociological 同根但更宽，泛指社会的
由 society 加形容词后缀构成，指整个社会层面的

senses.title: Relating to the discipline
senses.titleCN: 与社会学这门学科有关
senses.definition: belonging to or produced within the academic field of sociology
senses.definitionCN: 属于社会学领域或在该领域内产生的
senses.example: The journal published a sociological study of remote work.
senses.exampleCN: 该期刊发表了一项关于远程办公的社会学研究。
senses.why: The adjective is simply the discipline's name with its regular ending, so its first job is to attach things to the field.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词就是学科名加上常规词尾，因此它的第一项工作是把事物挂到这门学科上。

senses.title: Explaining by social structure
senses.definition: explaining an outcome through structures such as class, housing or institutions rather than personal choice
senses.definitionCN: 通过阶级、住房或制度等结构，而非个人选择，来解释某个结果
senses.example: A sociological account of dropout rates begins with catchment areas.
senses.exampleCN: 对辍学率的社会学解释，从学区划分开始。
senses.why: The discipline's main move is to shift the cause outward, so the adjective most often modifies explanation and account.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科的主要动作是把原因向外移，因此这个形容词最常修饰「解释」与「叙述」。

senses.title: Concerned with groups and institutions
senses.definition: focused on collectivities, organisations and shared practices rather than single persons
senses.definitionCN: 以集体、组织与共同实践为焦点，而非单个个人
senses.example: The sociological view treats a family budget as a product of wages and rents.
senses.exampleCN: 社会学视角把家庭预算看作工资与房租的产物。
senses.why: Once the unit of analysis is the group, the adjective marks that choice of unit.
senses.whyCN: 一旦分析单位是群体，这个形容词就标出这一选择。

senses.title: Using social-science methods
senses.definition: produced with surveys, interviews, observation or official statistics
senses.definitionCN: 通过调查、访谈、观察或官方统计得来的
senses.example: Her evidence was sociological rather than anecdotal: three thousand interviews.
senses.exampleCN: 她的证据是社会学的而非轶事式的：三千份访谈。
senses.why: Methods are what separate this adjective from mere social commentary, so it often appears before data and evidence.
senses.whyCN: 方法把这个形容词与单纯的社会评论区分开，因此它常出现在「数据」「证据」之前。

senses.title: Stressing collective causes
senses.definition: attributing outcomes to shared conditions instead of to individual effort or character
senses.definitionCN: 把结果归于共同处境，而不是个人努力或性格
senses.example: A sociological reading of absenteeism points to shift patterns, not laziness.
senses.exampleCN: 对缺勤的社会学解读指向轮班安排，而不是懒惰。
senses.why: The shift of blame from person to condition is the adjective's most contested use, and it is where arguments usually start.
senses.whyCN: 把责任从人移到处境，是这个形容词最有争议的用法，争论通常也从这里开始。

senses.title: Framing a private trouble as a public issue
senses.titleCN: 把个人困扰框定为公共议题
senses.definition: in the tradition of the sociological imagination, connecting personal difficulty to public arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 在社会学想象力的传统中，把个人困境与公共安排连起来
senses.example: The lecturer gave a sociological name to what students had felt as private failure.
senses.exampleCN: 讲师给学生们的私人挫败感起了一个社会学的名字。
senses.why: The most famous version of this move turns one person's unemployment into a question about how work is distributed.
senses.whyCN: 这一动作最著名的版本，是把一个人的失业变成关于工作如何分配的问题。

senses.title: Relating to a named subfield
senses.definition: describing work inside a specialised branch such as the sociology of medicine or of science
senses.definitionCN: 形容医学社会学或科学社会学等专门分支内的工作
senses.example: The sociological study of diagnosis compared two hospital wards.
senses.exampleCN: 关于诊断的社会学研究比较了两个医院病区。
senses.why: Every institution can be looked at this way, and each such look adds a compound to the adjective's range.
senses.whyCN: 每个制度都可以这样看，每一次这样的看都为这个形容词增加一个复合用法。

senses.title: Treating social facts as external constraints
senses.titleCN: 把社会事实视为外在约束
senses.definition: in the classic formulation, treating social facts as things that constrain individuals from outside
senses.definitionCN: 在经典表述中，把社会事实当作从外部约束个人的事物
senses.example: A sociological treatment of language policy treats the rules as external facts.
senses.exampleCN: 对语言政策的社会学处理把规则当作外在事实。
senses.why: The strongest form of the outward turn is to treat social arrangements as objects with force of their own.
senses.whyCN: 向外移最彻底的形态，是把社会安排当作自有力量的对象。

intro.en: Sociological is sociology plus the adjective ending -ical; the noun is a nineteenth-century compound of Latin and Greek. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: sociological 是 sociology 加形容词词尾；那个名词是十九世纪由拉丁语与希腊语构成的复合词。年代均为约数。

items.en: The root meant 'companion, ally', and its deeper origin is not established; a link to the verb for following is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 这个词根意为「同伴、盟友」，其更早来源未得到证明；把它与表「跟随」的动词相联系的说法只是假说。

items.en: The Greek element meant 'the study of' and had already built names such as biology and geology.
items.cn: 这个希腊成分意为「……之学」，此前已造出 biology、geology 一类名称。

items.en: The noun is generally attributed to Auguste Comte in the eighteen thirties, who wanted a science of society.
items.cn: 这个名词一般认为是孔德在十九世纪三十年代所造，他想要一门关于社会的科学。

items.en: The ending -ical is the ordinary English way of turning a Greek-derived discipline name into an adjective.
items.cn: 词尾是英语把希腊来源的学科名变成形容词的常规方式。

items.en: The adjective spread with the discipline in the twentieth century and now also describes any explanation that stresses social causes.
items.cn: 这个形容词在二十世纪随学科传播，如今也形容任何强调社会成因的解释。

items.en: Source uncertain (first printed use of the adjective and the origin of the companion word): the earliest citation is not settled, and the pre-Latin origin of the root is unknown, so any older form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（这个形容词的最早书证与「同伴」一词的来源）：最早用例尚无定论；该词根在拉丁语之前的来源亦不可考，凡为其提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds same-root adjectives that are easily confused; group two holds adjectives that also explain by structure.
note.cn: 第一组是同根形容词，极易混淆；第二组是同样以结构作解释的形容词。

entries.definition: Relating to society or to interaction; it can describe a party or a policy, while sociological points to the discipline or its style of explanation.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指与社会的或互动有关的，可形容聚会或政策；而 sociological 指学科或其解释风格。

entries.definition: Relating to society as a whole, often used for large-scale effects; it says nothing about the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 指整个社会层面的，常用于大规模影响，与学科无关。

entries.definition: The name of the field; the adjective modifies nouns, while this noun can be a subject or an object.
entries.definitionCN: 是领域之名；形容词修饰名词，而这个名词可作主语或宾语。

entries.definition: The practitioner; a sociological argument need not be made by a sociologist.
entries.definitionCN: 指从业者；一个社会学式论证未必由社会学者提出。

entries.definition: Relating to structure in any field, from engineering to economics; sociological specifies a social kind of structure.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何领域的结构，从工程到经济；sociological 限定为社会结构。

entries.definition: Relating to established organisations and rules; it is one favourite cause inside sociological explanation.
entries.definitionCN: 指与既有组织及规则有关的，是社会解释中最常用的一类成因。

entries.definition: Relating to the statistical makeup of a population; it supplies evidence rather than the whole explanation.
entries.definitionCN: 指与人口统计构成有关的，提供证据而非整全解释。

entries.definition: Relating to the study of cultures through close observation; it overlaps with sociological work but starts from culture.
entries.definitionCN: 指通过近距离观察研究文化的，与社会学工作重叠但以文化为起点。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real noun base, the real adjective ending and the real phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的名词基底、真实的形容词词尾与真实的短语。

normal.en: The adjective is the discipline name with its regular ending, so it means belonging to that field.
normal.cn: 这个形容词就是学科名加上常规词尾，因此意为「属于该领域」。

normal.en: Its most common job is to mark an explanation that moves the cause from the person to the arrangement.
normal.cn: 它最常见的用途，是标出一种把原因从人移到安排的说明。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: a sociological study, a sociological explanation, sociological factors.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：社会学研究、社会学解释、社会因素。

normal.en: The family runs society, social, societal, sociologist, sociology, sociological.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 society、social、societal、sociologist、sociology、sociological。

normal.en: The famous phrase sociological imagination names the move from a private trouble to a public issue.
normal.cn: 著名说法「社会学想象力」正是指从个人困扰移到公共议题的那一步。

abstract.en: Picture a room with one wall removed, showing the pipes shared with the whole street.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子被拆掉一面墙，露出与整条街共用的水管。

abstract.en: Picture a queue whose length is blamed on the timetable rather than on the people in it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条队伍，其长度被归因于时刻表而不是队伍里的人。

abstract.en: Picture a single cough heard as the sound of a whole building.
abstract.cn: 想象一声咳嗽被听成整栋楼的声音。

examples.en: The paper offers a sociological account of why the two districts diverged.
examples.cn: 这篇论文对两个街区为何分化给出了社会学解释。

examples.en: What looks like a personal habit is often a sociological pattern.
examples.cn: 看似个人习惯的东西，往往是社会学的模式。

examples.en: The course trains students to ask sociological questions about ordinary routines.
examples.cn: 这门课训练学生对日常惯例提出社会学问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「soci 同伴 + ological 学问的」——从人群与结构看问题的，就是社会学的

root: sociology（拉丁 socius「同伴」+ 希腊「……之学」）+ 形容词词尾；学科名一般认为是孔德所造；socius 更深来源不确定。英语 sociological。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one outward turn of the gaze: the cause is moved from the person to the arrangement. The adjective marks the field, the explanation, the group as unit, the methods, the collective cause, the private trouble made public, a named subfield, and finally social facts treated as external constraints.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿目光向外的一次转动展开：原因从人身上移到安排上。这个形容词依次标出学科、解释、以群体为单位、方法、集体成因、被公共化的个人困扰、命名分支，最后是被当作外在约束的社会事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a room with one wall removed, revealing pipes shared with the whole street.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间屋子被拆掉一面墙，露出与整条街共用的水管。

branches.en: THE FIELD AND ITS TOOLS: the discipline's name and the methods that make its claims systematic belong together.
branches.cn: 学科与工具：学科之名与使其主张成为系统的方法，同属一体。

branches.en: STRUCTURE AND UNIT: explaining by structure and choosing the group as the unit are two halves of the same outward turn.
branches.cn: 结构与单位：以结构作解释，与把群体定为分析单位，是同一向外转动的两半。

branches.en: CAUSES OUTSIDE THE PERSON: collective conditions and social facts with force of their own both press on the individual from outside.
branches.cn: 人之外的成因：共同处境与自有力量的社会事实，都从外部压向个人。

branches.en: PRIVATE MADE PUBLIC: a personal failure is renamed as a question about how things are arranged.
branches.cn: 私事公共化：个人的失败被改名成关于事物如何安排的问题。

branches.en: NAMED SUBFIELD: every institution studied this way adds a compound to the adjective's range.
branches.cn: 命名分支：每一个被这样研究的制度，都为这个形容词增添一个复合用法。

intro.en: The adjective is a Greek-derived discipline name plus the ordinary English adjective ending, with a Latin root underneath.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是一个希腊来源的学科名加常规英语形容词词尾，底下还有一个拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin socius gives society, social, associate and sociable; the Greek element recurs in biology, geology and theology.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 socius 衍生 society、social、associate 与 sociable；那个希腊成分还出现在 biology、geology 与 theology 中。

items.example: The root supplies the social half of the meaning.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供词义中「社会」那一半。

items.example: The element turns a root into a discipline name.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分把词根变成学科名。

items.example: The noun is the base of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是形容词的基底。

items.example: The ending is the standard way to make a discipline adjective in English.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾是英语中把学科名变成形容词的标准方式。

items.example: The adjective also covers any explanation that stresses social causes.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词也覆盖任何强调社会成因的解释。

items.example: The adverb marks an argument made from this angle.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词标出从这一角度作出的论证。

items.example: The adverb is common in research writing.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词在研究写作中很常见。

items.example: The person noun names the practitioner of the field.
items.exampleCN: 指人的名词指该领域的从业者。

items.example: A sociological claim can be made by anyone, not only by this person.
items.exampleCN: 社会学式主张任何人都能提出，不必出自这位从业者。

items.example: A shorter suffix produces the adjective for society as a whole.
items.exampleCN: 一个更短的后缀造出指整个社会的形容词。

definition_zh: 废除；尤指废除奴隶制；取消某项制度、法律或做法
definition_en: the formal ending of a system, law or practice, especially slavery
core_image: 一本旧法令被合上，封皮上的印章被划去，旁边是一截断裂的锁链
scene: 议事厅里，议员们把一叠旧法令搬到一边，书记在末页写下终止二字，旁听席上有人低声哭泣。 The abolition of the slave trade, its formal ending by law, forced merchants to rebuild their business.
sceneCN: 这里 abolition 指「正式废除一项制度」（第 1 个义项：以法律手段终止奴隶制一类制度）；句意为奴隶贸易的废除迫使商人重建自己的生意。可辨识物件：旧法令、印章、断裂锁链、议事厅长桌、旁听席。

pos.zh: 废除；废止（可数，复数 abolitions）

collocations.phrase: the abolition of the slave trade

derivatives.zh: 废奴主义者；主张废除者

senses.title: The formal ending of slavery
senses.definition: the legal termination of slavery as an institution
senses.definitionCN: 以法律终止奴隶制这一制度
senses.example: The abolition of the slave trade forced merchants to rebuild their business.
senses.exampleCN: 奴隶贸易的废除迫使商人重建自己的生意。
senses.why: abolere is 'to do away with, efface'; the noun names the act of making an institution cease to exist.
senses.whyCN: abolere 是「取消、抹去」；名词指使一项制度不复存在的行为。

senses.title: The abolition movement
senses.definition: the organised campaign that sought to end slavery and the slave trade
senses.definitionCN: 争取结束奴隶制与奴隶贸易的组织化运动
senses.example: Abolition grew from pamphlets into a mass campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 废奴运动从小册子发展成群众运动。
senses.why: a cause takes the name of its goal, so the abstract noun also labels the movement.
senses.whyCN: 事业以目标为名，因此这个抽象名词也标示运动。

senses.title: Repeal of a law or practice
senses.definition: the ending of a statute, rule or custom by the authority that made it
senses.definitionCN: 由制定机关终止一项法规、规则或惯例
senses.example: The abolition of the old tariff raised prices for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 旧关税的废除使价格升了一年。
senses.why: the word is not tied to slavery; any institution can be abolished, from a tax to a monarch.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不限于奴隶制；任何制度都可被废除，从税收到君主制。

senses.title: The repealing statute itself
senses.definition: the named act or instrument that declares an institution at an end
senses.definitionCN: 宣布某项制度终止的具名法案或文书
senses.example: The abolition act named a date for the change.
senses.exampleCN: 废除法案为这一变化指定了日期。
senses.why: legal English names the instrument by the result it produces, as with abolition.
senses.whyCN: 法律英语用结果来命名工具，abolition 就是如此。

senses.title: Gradual or partial abolition
senses.definition: the ending of one part of an institution before the rest, such as the trade before the institution
senses.definitionCN: 先终止制度的某一部分，再终止其余，如先废贸易再废制度
senses.example: Gradual abolition left a loophole for another decade.
senses.exampleCN: 逐步废除留下了另一个十年的漏洞。
senses.why: reform often moves by stages, so the noun takes modifiers such as gradual and partial.
senses.whyCN: 改革常分阶段推进，因此这个名词可带「逐步」「部分」等修饰语。

senses.title: International abolition
senses.definition: a worldwide agreement or norm ending a practice such as the death penalty or a weapon
senses.definitionCN: 终止死刑或某类武器等做法的全球性协定或规范
senses.example: International abolition of the trade required many treaties.
senses.exampleCN: 这一贸易的国际废除需要许多条约。
senses.why: some practices can only end across borders, so the noun gains a global scale.
senses.whyCN: 有些做法只能跨国终止，因此这个名词获得全球尺度。

senses.title: Abstraction: complete cancellation
senses.definition: any complete cancellation of a rule, custom or category, not only a legal one
senses.definitionCN: 任何对规则、惯例或类别的彻底取消，不限于法律
senses.example: The abolition of the weekly meeting surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 每周例会的取消让所有人意外。
senses.why: the core sense needs only a thing that exists and an authority that ends it.
senses.whyCN: 核心义只需要一物存在，以及一个权威将其终止。

senses.title: Metaphor: institutional disappearance
senses.definition: the disappearance of a structure so completely that later users no longer notice its absence
senses.definitionCN: 某一结构彻底消失，以致后来者不再察觉其缺失
senses.example: The abolition of that custom is visible only in old photographs.
senses.exampleCN: 那种习俗的废除只能从老照片里看出来。
senses.why: the deepest sense is erasure: not reform but the removal of the thing itself.
senses.whyCN: 最深的一层是抹除：不是改良，而是把事物本身移走。

intro.en: Abolition comes from Latin abolere 'to destroy, efface', through French. Its deeper formation is debated. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: abolition 经法语来自拉丁 abolere「摧毁、抹去」，其更深构词存在争论。年代均为约数。

items.en: Abolere meant 'to destroy, efface, cause to die out'; it is generally analysed as ab- 'away' plus olere 'to grow'.
items.cn: abolere 意为「摧毁、抹去、使消亡」；一般认为由 ab-「离开」加 olere「生长」构成。

items.en: Olere 'to grow' is related to alere 'to nourish'; the connection is generally accepted, while the deeper root remains uncertain and reconstructed.
items.cn: olere「生长」与 alere「滋养」相关；这一联系一般被接受，而其更深词根仍不确定，属重构。

items.en: Old French abolir carried the verb into English as abolish, and the noun abolition followed from the Latin action noun.
items.cn: 古法语 abolir 把动词带入英语作 abolish，名词 abolition 则来自拉丁行为名词。

items.en: Abolition entered English in the seventeenth century as a general word for doing away with something.
items.cn: abolition 在十七世纪进入英语，泛指取消某物。

items.en: From the late eighteenth century the word became the standard label for ending the slave trade and then slavery itself.
items.cn: 从十八世纪末起，这个词成为结束奴隶贸易、继而结束奴隶制本身的标准标签。

items.en: Source uncertain (the olere analysis): some dictionaries treat the ab- plus olere division as probable rather than certain, and the pre-Latin root of olere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（olere 的分析）：一些辞书把 ab- 加 olere 的划分视为「很可能」而非确定，olere 的拉丁语前词根属重构。

note.en: Group one holds abolish-family words that are easily confused with abolition; group two holds the neighbouring ideas of ending a rule.
note.cn: 第一组是易与 abolition 混淆的废除类词；第二组是终止规则的邻近概念。

entries.definition: To end an institution by authority; the noun names the act, the verb names the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 指由权威终止制度；名词指行为，动词指去做。

entries.definition: One who campaigns for abolition; it names the supporter, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指为废奴而奔走的人；命名支持者，而非行为。

entries.definition: A rarer noun for the same act; abolition is the established form in legal and historical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 指同一行为的较少见名词；abolition 是法律与历史写作中的通行形式。

entries.definition: Describing something that tends to abolish; it cannot replace the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 描述有废除倾向的事物；不能替代名词。

entries.definition: The formal cancellation of a law by the body that made it; narrower than abolition, which can end an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 指由制定机关正式取消一项法律；比 abolition 窄，后者可终止整个制度。

entries.definition: A declaration that something never had legal force, such as a marriage or contract; it looks backward, not forward.
entries.definitionCN: 指宣布某事物自始无效，如婚姻或合同；它向后看，而非向前。

entries.definition: The withdrawal of a licence, right or promise; it removes a permission rather than an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 指撤回许可、权利或承诺；移走的是许可，而非制度。

entries.definition: The freeing of persons from slavery or control; abolition ends the institution, emancipation changes the persons' status.
entries.definitionCN: 指使人脱离奴役或控制；abolition 终止制度，emancipation 改变人的身份。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the French verb, the antislavery campaign and the real legal compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：那个法语动词、废奴运动，以及真实的法条组合。

normal.en: ab- 'away' + olere 'grow': to cause something to grow away until it is gone.
normal.cn: ab-「离开」+ olere「生长」：使某物长到消失。

normal.en: The verb is abolish; the noun is abolition; the person is an abolitionist.
normal.cn: 动词是 abolish，名词是 abolition，人是 abolitionist。

normal.en: The family runs abolish, abolition, abolitionist, abolitionism, abolishable.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 abolish、abolition、abolitionist、abolitionism、abolishable。

normal.en: The cause is dated to the late eighteenth century, when the slave trade was attacked first.
normal.cn: 这场事业定在十八世纪末，最先受攻击的是奴隶贸易。

normal.en: Typical partners are slavery, slave trade, capital punishment, gradual.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是奴隶制、奴隶贸易、死刑与「逐步」。

abstract.en: Picture a word removed from a dictionary so that later readers never meet it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词被从词典里移除，后来的读者再也遇不到它。

abstract.en: Picture a road erased and grass growing where the traffic used to be.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路被抹去，旧日车流处长出草。

abstract.en: Picture a chair taken out of a room; the space remains, but nothing fills it.
abstract.cn: 想象一把椅子被搬出房间；空间还在，却空无一物。

examples.en: Abolition was achieved only after decades of petitioning.
examples.cn: 经过数十年的请愿，废除才得以实现。

examples.en: The abolition of that tax changed how the port was funded.
examples.cn: 那项税的废除改变了港口的资金来源。

examples.en: Historians debate whether abolition helped the workers it was meant to save.
examples.cn: 历史学家争论废奴是否帮助了它本应拯救的工人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ab（离开）+ olish（完成）」——让制度离开并做到底 → 废除

root: 拉丁 abolere「摧毁、抹去」，一般认为由 ab-（离开）+ olere（生长）构成；olere 与 alere「滋养」相关，更深词根属重构。名词 abolitio 经法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one erasure: an authority makes an institution cease to exist. The erasure becomes slavery's ending, a movement, a repealed statute, the act itself, staged reform, a global norm, any cancellation and finally a disappearance no longer noticed.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一次抹除展开：权威使一项制度不再存在。这次抹除先成为奴隶制的终结，再成为运动、被废的法令、法令本身、分阶段改革、全球规范、任何取消，最后成为不再被察觉的消失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old statute closed, its seal struck through, a broken chain beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本旧法令被合上，印章被划去，旁边一截断链。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION AND THE CAUSE: ending slavery and the campaign that demanded it share one word.
branches.cn: 制度与事业：终止奴隶制与要求它的运动共用一个词。

branches.en: THE RULE AND THE PAPER: a practice ends, and an act records the ending.
branches.cn: 规则与纸面：惯例终止，法案记录这次终止。

branches.en: THE STAGES: reform can be gradual at home and global abroad.
branches.cn: 阶段：改革可在国内逐步，也可在国际上铺开。

branches.en: ANY CANCELLATION: a meeting, a tax or a category can be abolished.
branches.cn: 任何取消：会议、税项或类别都可被废除。

branches.en: THE ERASURE: the deepest sense is a structure gone so fully that its absence is invisible.
branches.cn: 抹除：最深的一层是结构彻底消失，连缺失都看不见。

intro.en: Abolition is a Latin verb turned noun, carried through French, with a root that also underlies words about growth.
intro.cn: abolition 是由拉丁动词转成的名词，经法语进入英语，其词根也构成若干表示「生长」的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin abolere gives abolish and abolition; the related olere and alere line gives adult and adolescent, where growth is literal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 abolere 衍生 abolish 与 abolition；相关的 olere 与 alere 一线衍生 adult 与 adolescent，那里的「生长」仍是字面的。

items.example: The prefix marks removal from existence.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出「从存在中移除」。

items.example: The root contributes the image of growth.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「生长」的意象。

items.meaning: to cause to grow away, destroy
items.example: The verb pictured a thing wasting away to nothing.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描绘事物消退至无。

items.example: The abolitionist printed a weekly paper.
items.exampleCN: 这位废奴主义者印行一份周报。

items.meaningCN: 主张废除奴隶制的主义

items.example: Not every custom is abolishable by law.
items.exampleCN: 并非每种习俗都能由法律废除。

items.structure: adult (Latin adultus, grown up, from adolescere)
items.example: The word shares the growth image, not the abolition sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个词共享「生长」意象，但不含废除义。

definition_zh: 强制的；胁迫的；用武力迫使的
definition_en: using pressure, threats or force to make someone act against their own preference
core_image: 一扇门被从外面顶住，里面的人只能往唯一的方向退
scene: 会议室里没有人投反对票，因为先前反对的人已经被请出去了。 The agreement was coercive rather than freely negotiated.
sceneCN: 这里 coercive 指以强制手段迫使对方接受（第 1 个义项：以强制迫使人行动）；句意为这份协议是强制达成的，而不是自由谈成的。

senses.title: Forcing someone to act
senses.definition: using pressure, threats or force to make a person act against their preference
senses.definitionCN: 以压力、威胁或武力使某人违背自己意愿行事
senses.example: The agreement was coercive rather than freely negotiated.
senses.exampleCN: 这份协议是强制达成的，而不是自由谈成的。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to shut in together': the pressured person is given no room to move except the one chosen by the other side.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「一起关起来」：被施压者除了对方选定的方向之外，没有可移动的余地。

senses.title: Backed by penalties
senses.definition: of a rule or measure, enforced by penalties rather than by persuasion
senses.definitionCN: 指规则或措施靠惩罚而非说服来执行
senses.example: The city imposed coercive fines on illegal dumping.
senses.exampleCN: 该市对非法倾倒处以强制罚款。
senses.why: A rule without a penalty is advice; the penalty is what closes the exit and makes the rule coercive.
senses.whyCN: 没有惩罚的规则只是建议；惩罚封住出口，才使规则具有强制性。

senses.title: Power that punishes
senses.definition: in politics, power resting on the ability to punish or deprive
senses.definitionCN: 在政治学中，指建立在惩罚或剥夺能力之上的权力
senses.example: The regime relied on coercive power rather than legitimacy.
senses.exampleCN: 该政权依靠强制力而非合法性。
senses.why: Power can persuade, reward or punish; the coercive kind works by making refusal expensive.
senses.whyCN: 权力可以说服、给予或惩罚；强制性的那一种通过让拒绝变得昂贵来起作用。

senses.title: A pressuring tone
senses.definition: of speech, pressing the listener rather than inviting a response
senses.definitionCN: 指言语压迫听者，而不是邀请回应
senses.example: His coercive tone ended the discussion before it began.
senses.exampleCN: 他带有压迫感的语气让讨论还没开始就结束了。
senses.why: Tone can close a conversation the way a fine closes a road; the listener is still present but has no way through.
senses.whyCN: 语气可以像罚款封路那样封住对话；听者仍在场，却无路可走。

senses.title: Bargaining under threat
senses.definition: of negotiation, conducted while one side holds a threat over the other
senses.definitionCN: 指谈判在一方对另一方持有威胁的情况下进行
senses.example: The strike turned the talks into coercive bargaining.
senses.exampleCN: 罢工把谈判变成了胁迫性谈判。
senses.why: A bargain assumes both sides may walk away; a threat removes that option, so the agreement is signed under pressure.
senses.whyCN: 交易假定双方都可以走开；威胁移除了这个选项，于是协议在压力下签署。

senses.title: Involuntary treatment
senses.definition: in psychiatry or law, treatment given without the patient's consent
senses.definitionCN: 在精神医学或法律中，未经病人同意而给予的治疗
senses.example: The court authorized coercive treatment for the patient.
senses.exampleCN: 法院批准对该病人实施强制治疗。
senses.why: When a person cannot consent safely, the law may replace consent with authority, and the word marks that substitution.
senses.whyCN: 当一个人无法安全地作出同意时，法律可能用权威取代同意，而这个词标记的正是这种取代。

senses.title: Forced recruitment
senses.definition: of recruitment, compelling people into service against their will
senses.definitionCN: 指违背本人意愿迫使人们服役
senses.example: Coercive recruitment filled the ranks with unwilling soldiers.
senses.exampleCN: 强制征募用不情愿的士兵填满了队伍。
senses.why: A volunteer army relies on choice; conscription replaces choice with a penalty for refusal, which is the definition of coercion.
senses.whyCN: 志愿军依靠选择；征兵用「拒绝即受罚」取代选择，这正是强制的定义。

senses.title: An environment with no real exit
senses.definition: of a setting or relationship, where refusing carries a cost that makes consent nominal
senses.definitionCN: 指环境或关系中，拒绝要付出代价，使「同意」只是名义上的
senses.example: The workers described a coercive environment with no real exit.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们描述了一个没有真实退路的强制环境。
senses.why: The last sense is structural: nothing is said aloud, but every option except one has been quietly priced out.
senses.whyCN: 最后一个义项是结构性的：没有任何明说，但除了一种选择之外，其余选择都被悄然标上了高昂代价。

intro.en: Coercive comes from a Latin verb meaning to shut in or restrain, built from 'together' and 'enclose'.
intro.cn: coercive 来自一个意为「关起来、约束」的拉丁动词，由「一起」与「围住」构成。

items.en: English formed coercive in the 17c. from coercion, and modern politics uses it for power that punishes.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪由 coercion 造出 coercive；现代政治学用它指以惩罚为基础的权力。

items.en: Coercere meant 'to shut in, restrain, compel', formed from co- 'together' and arcere 'to enclose, keep off'.
items.cn: coercere 意为「关住、约束、强迫」，由 co-「一起」与 arcere「围住、挡住」构成。

items.en: Arcere 'to enclose, ward off' also underlies the noun arx, a citadel, and the English word arcane through a different path.
items.cn: arcere「围住、挡开」也构成名词 arx（城堡），并通过另一条路径与英语 arcane 相关。

items.en: Roman law used coercitio for the magistrate's power to compel obedience by fines and arrest.
items.cn: 罗马法用 coercitio 指长官通过罚款与拘捕强制服从的权力。

items.en: The word widened from courts to workplaces and families, where pressure can compel without any visible force.
items.cn: 这个词从法庭扩展到职场与家庭，在这些地方，压力无需可见的武力也能迫使行动。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the coercion stem; the near-meaning group names kinds of compulsion.
note.cn: 形近组共享 coercion 词干；近义组列出各种强迫。

entries.definition: the act of compelling someone by pressure or force.
entries.definitionCN: 以压力或武力强迫他人的行为。

entries.definition: in a way that compels someone.
entries.definitionCN: 以强迫他人的方式。

entries.definition: to compel a person to act against their will.
entries.definitionCN: 强迫某人违背意愿行事。

entries.definition: capable of being compelled.
entries.definitionCN: 可被强迫的。

entries.definition: brought about by pressure rather than free choice.
entries.definitionCN: 由压力而非自由选择造成。

entries.definition: required by rule or law, with penalties for refusal.
entries.definitionCN: 由规则或法律要求，拒绝受罚。

entries.definition: ordered by an authority and not optional.
entries.definitionCN: 由权威命令，不可选择。

entries.definition: unjustly harsh and hard to resist.
entries.definitionCN: 不公正地严苛且难以抗拒。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a door held shut from outside.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「门从外面被顶住」的画面留住。

normal.en: co means together, arcere means to enclose: coercive pressure closes the exits.

normal.en: Picture a door held shut from the outside while someone waits within.
normal.cn: 想象门从外面被顶住，里面的人在等。

normal.en: A penalty is the lock on the door; without it a rule is only a request.
normal.cn: 惩罚是门上的锁；没有它，规则只是请求。

normal.en: Say co-ER-sive, with the stress on the closing motion.
normal.cn: 读成 co-ER-sive，重音落在「关闭」的动作上。

normal.en: Link it with coerce: the verb is the act, the adjective is the quality of the act.
normal.cn: 把它和 coerce 联系：动词是行为，形容词是行为性质。

abstract.en: Consent under a threat is consent in name only.
abstract.cn: 威胁之下的同意只是名义上的同意。

abstract.en: Power that punishes works by making refusal expensive.
abstract.cn: 以惩罚为基础的权力，通过让拒绝变得昂贵来运作。

abstract.en: The quietest coercion is an environment where only one option is affordable.
abstract.cn: 最安静的强制，是一个只有一种选择付得起的处境。

examples.en: The agreement was coercive rather than freely negotiated.
examples.cn: 这份协议是强制达成的，而不是自由谈成的。

examples.en: The regime relied on coercive power rather than legitimacy.
examples.cn: 该政权依靠强制力而非合法性。

examples.en: The workers described a coercive environment with no real exit.
examples.cn: 工人们描述了一个没有真实退路的强制环境。

dict_mnemonic.text: co（一起）+ erc（围住）+ ive：把人围住、封住出口，就是「强制的」。

root: 拉丁语 coercere（关住、强迫）：co-（一起）+ arcere（围住、挡住）

sensesIntro.en: Coercive always closes an exit; the senses differ in what the exit is, whether a legal penalty, a threat, a treatment order or the cost of refusal.
sensesIntro.cn: coercive 始终在封住某个出口；各义项的差别在于出口是什么，是法律惩罚、威胁、治疗令，还是拒绝的代价。

core.en: THE EXIT IS CLOSED
core.cn: 出口被关上

branches.en: The act of compulsion and the tone that carries it.
branches.cn: 强迫行为以及承载它的语气。

branches.en: Penalties and power that rest on punishment.
branches.cn: 惩罚以及以惩罚为基础的权力。

branches.en: Negotiation conducted under a threat.
branches.cn: 在威胁之下进行的谈判。

branches.en: Treatment and service imposed without consent.
branches.cn: 未经同意施加的治疗与服役。

branches.en: The structural case, where every other option is priced out.
branches.cn: 结构性情形，其他选择都被代价排除。

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb stem with an English adjective ending, and its relatives keep the image of enclosure.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁动词词干加英语形容词词尾，其同族词保留「围住」意象。

latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁语条目展示「关住」如何变成「强迫」。

items.meaning: tending to shut in or compel
items.example: The law is coercive in effect.
items.exampleCN: 这项法律在效果上具有强制性。

definition_zh: 结晶；使结晶；（想法、计划）变得明确；裹糖（糖渍）
definition_en: to form crystals or cause something to form crystals; to become or make something clear and definite
core_image: 作坊里，裹了糖的姜片摊在竹筛上晾干，糖层慢慢结成白色颗粒
scene: 作坊里，师傅把煮好的姜片裹上糖，摊在竹筛上晾干，糖层慢慢结成白色颗粒。 The ginger slices crystallize as the sugar syrup cools around them.
sceneCN: 这里 crystallize 指「（糖浆在表面）结晶、形成糖霜」（第 5 个义项：用糖包裹并使其结晶，即糖渍）；句意为糖浆在姜片周围冷却时，姜片逐渐结晶挂霜。可辨识物件：竹筛、糖渍姜片、白色糖霜、冷却的糖浆。

senses.title: Form crystals (intransitive)
senses.definition: of a substance: to separate from a liquid as ordered solid crystals
senses.definitionCN: 指物质从液体中析出为有序固体晶体
senses.example: The ginger slices crystallize as the sugar syrup cools around them.
senses.exampleCN: 糖浆在姜片周围冷却时，姜片逐渐结晶挂霜。
senses.why: The intransitive use describes the substance acting on its own.
senses.whyCN: 不及物用法描述物质自身发生的变化。

senses.title: Cause crystals to form
senses.definition: to make a dissolved substance form crystals, as by cooling or seeding
senses.definitionCN: 指通过降温或加晶种使溶解物形成晶体
senses.example: Chemists crystallize the compound by cooling its saturated solution.
senses.exampleCN: 化学家通过冷却饱和溶液使化合物结晶。
senses.why: The transitive use adds an agent who cools or seeds the solution.
senses.whyCN: 及物用法增加一个降温或加晶种的施事。

senses.title: Become definite
senses.definition: of plans or ideas: to take a clear and fixed form after being vague
senses.definitionCN: 指计划或想法从模糊变得清晰固定
senses.example: Their vague proposal crystallized into a detailed scheme.
senses.exampleCN: 他们含糊的提议具体成了一项详细方案。
senses.why: Plans become definite the way crystals become solid.
senses.whyCN: 计划变明确，正如晶体变固体。

senses.title: Make something definite
senses.definition: to give a clear and fixed form to an idea, plan or movement
senses.definitionCN: 指使想法、计划或运动取得清晰固定的形态
senses.example: The speech crystallized the demands of the movement.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇演说把这场运动的要求明确固定下来。
senses.why: An agent can make an idea definite, matching the transitive pattern.
senses.whyCN: 施事可以使想法变明确，与及物模式相合。

senses.title: Coat and preserve with sugar
senses.definition: to coat fruit or peel with sugar syrup that then crystallizes
senses.definitionCN: 指用糖浆包裹水果或果皮，并使糖层结晶
senses.example: They crystallize orange peel for the holiday market.
senses.exampleCN: 他们糖渍橙皮供应节日市场。
senses.why: Sugar coating is literal crystallization on a fruit's surface.
senses.whyCN: 裹糖就是字面意义上的结晶发生在果皮表面。

senses.title: Freeze into ice crystals
senses.definition: of water: to turn into ice crystals, especially in food or tissue
senses.definitionCN: 指水结成冰晶，尤指在食品或组织中
senses.example: Water crystallizes in the cells and bursts them.
senses.exampleCN: 水在细胞里结晶，把细胞胀破。
senses.why: Water in cells crystallizes and expands, which is why it bursts them.
senses.whyCN: 细胞里的水结晶并膨胀，这正是它胀破细胞的原因。

senses.title: Separate out as crystals
senses.definition: to come out of a solution as solid crystals, often with 'out'
senses.definitionCN: 指从溶液中以固体晶体形式析出，常与 out 连用
senses.example: The salt crystallized out as the water evaporated.
senses.exampleCN: 水蒸发时盐结晶析出。
senses.why: The particle out marks separation from solution.
senses.whyCN: 小品词 out 标记从溶液中分离出来。

senses.title: Develop into a clear form
senses.definition: to develop into a recognizable and organized form, often with 'into'
senses.definitionCN: 指发展成可辨识、有组织的形态，常与 into 连用
senses.example: The protest crystallized into a national campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 这场抗议发展成一场全国性运动。
senses.why: The particle into marks development into a recognized form.
senses.whyCN: 小品词 into 标记发展为可辨识的形态。

intro.en: Crystallize is an English verb coined on crystal with the Latin-derived suffix -ize, following the pattern of French and Latin verbs in -iser and -izare.
intro.cn: crystallize 是在 crystal 上加拉丁来源后缀 -ize 构成的英语动词，仿照法语 -iser 与拉丁 -izare 的动词模式。

items.en: Krystallos 'ice, rock crystal' gave Latin crystallus and English crystal.
items.cn: krystallos「冰、水晶」产生拉丁 crystallus 与英语 crystal。

items.en: Latin -izare, from Greek -izein, formed verbs meaning 'to make or become'; it entered English through French -iser.
items.cn: 拉丁 -izare（源自希腊 -izein）构成表示「使……、成为……」的动词，经法语 -iser 进入英语。

items.en: The verb appears in seventeenth-century chemical writing for the formation of salt crystals from solution.
items.cn: 这个动词在十七世纪化学文献中出现，指盐从溶液中形成晶体。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geology applied the verb to minerals forming from cooling magma and to ice forming in rock cracks.
items.cn: 十九世纪地质学把这个动词用于矿物从冷却岩浆中形成，以及岩石裂隙中冰的形成。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries crystallize became a common figure for ideas and movements taking definite shape.
items.cn: 在十九、二十世纪，crystallize 成为想法与运动取得明确形态的常用比喻。

items.en: Not uncertain: the formation from crystal plus -ize is transparent. Only the exact first date of the figurative use is approximate.
items.cn: 并非存疑：由 crystal 加 -ize 构成这一点清楚可读。仅比喻义的准确首次年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds verbs that look like crystallize but differ in root or spelling; group two holds verbs for becoming solid or definite.
note.cn: 第一组是外形近似但词根或拼写不同的动词；第二组是表示变硬或变明确的动词。

entries.definition: The British spelling with -ise; it is the same verb, not a different process.
entries.definitionCN: 英式拼写，用 -ise；是同一个动词，不是另一过程。

entries.definition: To burn tissue to stop bleeding, from Greek kautēr 'branding iron'; it shares the ending only.
entries.definitionCN: 指烧灼组织以止血，来自希腊 kautēr「烙铁」；只共享词尾。

entries.definition: The noun from which the verb is formed; it names the object that results, not the action that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 构成该动词的名词；它命名产生的结果对象，而非产生它的动作。

entries.definition: The past participle and adjective, as in crystallized fruit; it names the result, not the action.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词兼形容词，如糖渍水果；它命名结果而非动作。

entries.definition: The general verb for turning liquid into solid; crystallize adds the idea of ordered growth.
entries.definitionCN: 指液体变固体的总称；crystallize 增加有序生长之意。

entries.definition: To come out of a solution as a solid, often without crystal order; a chemical rather than a structural emphasis.
entries.definitionCN: 指从溶液中析出固体，常无晶体秩序；强调化学而非结构。

entries.definition: To become hard or firm, without saying anything about internal order.
entries.definitionCN: 指变硬变坚，不涉及内部秩序。

entries.definition: An idiom for a plan or idea becoming definite; crystallize is its more formal single-word equivalent.
entries.definitionCN: 指计划或想法变明确的口语说法；crystallize 是更正式的单词对应。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix, the real phrasal verbs and the real confectionery use.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的后缀、真实的短语动词与真实的糖渍用法。

normal.en: Crystal plus -ize: to make or become crystal, exactly as the suffix says.
normal.cn: crystal 加 -ize：使成晶体或成为晶体，正如后缀所示。

normal.en: Two phrasal verbs carry much of the meaning: crystallize out and crystallize into.
normal.cn: 两个短语动词承载了大部分词义：结晶析出与具体形成为。

normal.en: The family runs crystal, crystalline, crystallize, crystallization, crystallized.
normal.cn: 词族包括 crystal、crystalline、crystallize、crystallization、crystallized。

normal.en: In the kitchen the verb means candied: crystallized ginger, crystallized peel.
normal.cn: 在厨房里这个动词指糖渍：糖姜片、糖橙皮。

normal.en: In writing it means making an idea sharp: a speech crystallizes demands.
normal.cn: 在写作中它指使想法锐利：一篇演说把要求明确下来。

abstract.en: Picture a fog that suddenly knows what shape it wants to be.
abstract.cn: 想象一片雾突然知道自己想成为什么形状。

abstract.en: Picture an argument freezing into a single clear sentence.
abstract.cn: 想象一场争论冻结成一句清楚的话。

abstract.en: Picture sugar putting on armour one grain at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象糖一粒一粒地穿上盔甲。

examples.en: Salt crystallizes out when the brine is concentrated.
examples.cn: 盐水浓缩时盐结晶析出。

examples.en: The movement crystallized into a political party within a year.
examples.cn: 这场运动在一年内发展成一个政党。

examples.en: Crystallized ginger is sold in small paper bags.
examples.cn: 糖姜片装在小纸袋里出售。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克瑞斯（crystal）来（li）z」——让东西像水晶那样定形 → 结晶、明确

root: crystal（希腊 krystallos「冰、水晶」）+ -ize（拉丁 -izare，源自希腊 -izein，使……、成为……）→ crystallize「使结晶；使明确」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one verb in two directions: matter forms crystals, and ideas form shapes, with sugar, ice, solutions and movements each taking part.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让一个动词朝两个方向展开：物质结成晶体，想法结成形体，糖、冰、溶液与运动各自参与其中。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: syrup drying into a hard white coat on a slice of ginger.
core.cn: 核心意象：糖浆在姜片上晾成一层硬白霜。

branches.en: MAKE AND BECOME: the verb works both without and with an object.
branches.cn: 使然与自然：这个动词既可不及物，也可及物。

branches.en: THE IDEA SETS: vague proposals harden into schemes and demands.
branches.cn: 想法定形：含糊的提议硬化为方案与要求。

branches.en: KITCHEN AND ICE: sugar and water both crystallize on a surface or in a cell.
branches.cn: 厨房与冰：糖与水都会在表面或细胞内结晶。

branches.en: OUT OF SOLUTION: the technical phrasal verb for material leaving a liquid as solid.
branches.cn: 从溶液中析出：物质以固体离开液体的技术短语。

branches.en: INTO A FORM: a movement develops a recognizable body.
branches.cn: 成为形态：一场运动发展出可辨识的躯体。

intro.en: Crystallize is a noun plus a verb-forming suffix, and the suffix is shared with hundreds of English verbs.
intro.cn: crystallize 是名词加动词后缀，这个后缀与数百个英语动词共享。

latinIntro.en: Latin crystallus gives the base; -izare, from Greek -izein, gives the verb pattern seen in organize, realize and crystallize.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 crystallus 提供词基；-izare（源自希腊 -izein）提供 organize、realize、crystallize 中的动词模式。

items.exampleCN: 这个词干命名有序固体。

definition_zh: 嗜酒的；爱灌酒的；吸水的；易透水的
definition_en: fond of drinking alcohol; absorbent, able to soak up liquid
core_image: 一端是举杯不放手的老酒客，一端是喝饱墨水的厚纸
scene: 宴席散场，他还扶着吧台不肯走。 The bibulous uncle told the same story three times.
sceneCN: 这里 bibulous 是「嗜酒的、贪杯的」（第 1 个义项：好酒贪杯）；句意是贪杯的舅舅把同一个故事讲了三遍。

derivatives.zh: bibulous 加 -ly，义为「嗜酒地；吸水地」
bibulous 加 -ness，义为「嗜酒；吸水性」
同根动词，义为「喝；饮；吸收」

senses.title: Fond of drinking alcohol
senses.definition: given to drinking a lot of alcohol, often cheerfully
senses.definitionCN: 好饮大量酒类，常带乐呵呵的劲头
senses.example: The bibulous uncle told the same story three times.
senses.exampleCN: 贪杯的舅舅把同一个故事讲了三遍。
senses.why: Latin bibere means to drink, so the drinker gets the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 bibere 意为「喝」，爱喝之人便得了这个形容词。

senses.title: Absorbent of liquid
senses.definition: highly absorbent, soaking up liquid readily
senses.definitionCN: 极易吸收液体，如纸或土壤
senses.example: Bibulous paper blotted the spilled ink at once.
senses.exampleCN: 吸水纸立刻吸干了洒出的墨水。
senses.why: Paper, like a toper, drinks up everything poured.
senses.whyCN: 纸张如酒客，倒多少喝多少。

senses.title: Of convivial drinking occasions
senses.definition: marked by much convivial drinking
senses.definitionCN: 以热闹豪饮为特色的
senses.example: Their club held a bibulous annual dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的俱乐部每年举办酒酣耳热的晚宴。
senses.why: The drinkers' mood spreads to the whole gathering.
senses.whyCN: 酒客的兴致弥漫至整场聚会。

senses.title: Sozzled, tipsy
senses.definition: merrily drunk or tipsy
senses.definitionCN: 喝得微醺或醉态可掬
senses.example: The bibulous crowd sang through the night.
senses.exampleCN: 醉醺醺的人群唱了一整夜。
senses.why: From loving drink to being full of it is a short step.
senses.whyCN: 从贪杯到灌满，一步之遥。

senses.title: Permeable, letting liquid through
senses.definition: permitting liquid to pass or soak through easily
senses.definitionCN: 允许液体轻易渗过
senses.example: The bibulous wall took paint unevenly.
senses.exampleCN: 渗水性强的墙面吃漆不匀。
senses.why: A surface that drinks liquid takes stain as a toper takes wine.
senses.whyCN: 喝液体的表面，吃色如酒客吃酒。

senses.title: Spongy in texture
senses.definition: soft and spongy, like material that drinks in moisture
senses.definitionCN: 质地柔软多孔，如吸湿材料
senses.example: The bibulous cloth wrung out heavy and dark.
senses.exampleCN: 那块吸饱水的布拧出来又沉又黑。
senses.why: Sponge-like matter is the paper sense extended.
senses.whyCN: 海绵质是吸水义的延伸。

senses.title: Absorbing like a habitual drinker (figurative)
senses.definition: greedily taking in information or influence, as if drinking
senses.definitionCN: 贪婪吸收信息或影响，如同畅饮
senses.example: She read with bibulous appetite, devouring every review.
senses.exampleCN: 她如饥似渴地读，连每篇书评都不放过。
senses.why: Drinking imagery turns intellectual when applied to reading.
senses.whyCN: 饮的意象落到阅读上，便成了求知如渴。

senses.title: Humorous, formal label for tipplers
senses.definition: a formal or jocular way to call someone a habitual drinker
senses.definitionCN: 以书面诙谐语气称人好酒成性
senses.example: The essay sketched the town's most bibulous citizens.
senses.exampleCN: 文章勾画了镇上最好酒的一群人物。
senses.why: Learned Latin dress makes the drinking joke polished.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁腔的学究外衣，让酒话也显得文雅。

definition_en: to belong or relate to something, especially as a right or duty proper to it
core_image: 系在主人身上：权利像链子一样拴在身份或职位上
scene: 老律师翻开地契，指着一行小字讲解权利的归属。 These grazing rights appertain to the owner of the hillside.
sceneCN: 这里 appertain 是「属于、随附于」（第 1 个义项：权利归属）；句意为：这些放牧权属于山坡的所有人。
