senses.title: To belong as a right
senses.definition: to belong to someone as a legal or rightful possession
senses.definitionCN: 作为法定或正当的归属而属于某人
senses.example: The title and its privileges appertain to the eldest son.
senses.exampleCN: 头衔及其特权属于长子。
senses.why: The root tenere means to hold, so rights are pictured as held onto their owner.
senses.whyCN: 词根 tenere 意为握持，权利被想象为紧握在所有者手中。

senses.title: To relate to a subject
senses.definition: to have a connection with a topic or matter
senses.definitionCN: 与某一话题或事项有联系
senses.example: All documents appertaining to the sale were archived.
senses.exampleCN: 与销售有关的所有文件都归了档。
senses.why: Things held together belong to the same cluster of meaning.
senses.whyCN: 被一并握持的东西属于同一意义群。

senses.title: To attach to a position or status
senses.definition: to attach naturally to an office, rank, or role
senses.definitionCN: 天然地附着于某一职位、等级或角色
senses.example: Duties appertain to every office.
senses.exampleCN: 每个职位都自带职责。
senses.why: A role holds its own duties, just as a hand holds tools.
senses.whyCN: 角色握有自己的职责，正如手握着工具。

senses.title: To be proper or fitting
senses.definition: to be appropriate to a person or thing in character
senses.definitionCN: 在性质上与某人某物相称
senses.example: Silence appertains to grief.
senses.exampleCN: 沉默与悲哀相称。
senses.why: What belongs to a thing fits its nature, yielding the propriety sense.
senses.whyCN: 属于某物的就是合其本性的，于是产生相称义。

senses.title: To concern a person indirectly
senses.definition: to touch upon someone's interests without directly involving them
senses.definitionCN: 涉及某人利益但不直接牵连其本人
senses.example: The rumor appertains to her family, not to her.
senses.exampleCN: 传言涉及她的家人，而非她本人。
senses.why: A held thread can lead outward to nearby interests.
senses.whyCN: 被握住的线头可以牵到临近的利益上。

senses.title: To form part of a system
senses.definition: to be one of the elements held within a larger set
senses.definitionCN: 作为更大集合中的一员
senses.example: These rituals appertain to the old religion.
senses.exampleCN: 这些仪式属于旧宗教的一部分。
senses.why: The system holds its parts the way a circle holds its points.
senses.whyCN: 系统握住各部分，如同圆握住它的点。

senses.title: To pertain in legal use
senses.definition: in law, to attach to property or an estate as an incident
senses.definitionCN: 法律上作为附属事项附着于财产或地产
senses.example: Easements appertain to the dominant land.
senses.exampleCN: 地役权附着于需役地。
senses.why: Law fixes holding into formal ownership, sharpening the root image.
senses.whyCN: 法律把「握持」固化为正式的所有，强化了词根意象。

senses.title: To follow from a quality
senses.definition: to result from or accompany an inherent quality
senses.definitionCN: 由内在性质引发或相伴而生
senses.example: Respect appertains to wisdom.
senses.exampleCN: 敬重随智慧而生。
senses.why: Qualities hold their consequences, like a root holds its fruit.
senses.whyCN: 性质握有自己的结果，如同根握着果。

intro.en: Appertain comes from Latin pertinere, to reach through to, hence to belong, from per- plus tenere.
intro.cn: appertain 来自拉丁语 pertinere（贯穿而达，引申为属于），由 per- 加 tenere 构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root *ten- meant to stretch or extend.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ten- 意为伸展、延伸。

items.en: Tenere meant to hold; per- added the idea of thoroughness, so pertinere meant to extend right through.
items.cn: tenere 意为握持；per- 增加彻底之意，pertinere 即「贯穿延伸」。

items.en: Pertinere shifted to mean to belong or relate, the image of a chain held at both ends.
items.cn: pertinere 转义为「属于、相关」，如两端被握住的链条。

items.en: English formed appertain in the fourteenth century from pertain with the Latin-style prefix ap-.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪在 pertain 上加拉丁风格前缀 ap- 构成 appertain。

items.en: It survives mainly in formal and legal writing, meaning to belong or relate to.
items.cn: 如今主要见于正式与法律文体，意为属于或与……有关。

note.en: Appertain belongs to the ten-family of holding words and stands near several belong-words.
note.cn: appertain 属于 ten「握持」词族，并与若干「属于」类词相邻。

entries.definition: to relate or belong to something
entries.definitionCN: 关于；属于

entries.definition: directly relevant to the matter at hand
entries.definitionCN: 切题的；相关的

entries.definition: to keep in possession
entries.definitionCN: 保留；保持

entries.definition: to be the property or proper part of something
entries.definitionCN: 属于；是……的正当部分

entries.definition: to have a connection with
entries.definitionCN: 与……有联系

entries.definition: to be about or affect
entries.definitionCN: 涉及；关系到

normalIntro.en: Anchor appertain in the ten-family of holding words.
normalIntro.cn: 把 appertain 锚定在 ten「握持」词族上。

normal.en: appertain = ap- (toward) + tain (hold): held toward its owner.
normal.cn: appertain = ap-（朝向）+ tain（握持）：被握向它的主人。

normal.en: Same root as contain, retain, obtain — all about holding.
normal.cn: 与 contain、retain、obtain 同根——都关乎握持。

normal.en: Classic pattern: rights appertain to the office.
normal.cn: 经典句式：rights appertain to the office（权利随职位而来）。

normal.en: pertain is the plainer twin; appertain is the legal, formal one.
normal.cn: pertain 是朴素的孪生词；appertain 更法律化、更正式。

normal.en: pertinent, the adjective cousin, means relevant.
normal.cn: 形容词亲戚 pertinent 意为切题的。

abstract.en: A crown held in a firm grip — the grip is who it appertains to.
abstract.cn: 一只手紧握王冠——握住的那只手就是它的归属。

abstract.en: A chain linking a key to a belt: the key appertains to the belt.
abstract.cn: 链条把钥匙拴在腰带上：钥匙属于腰带。

abstract.en: Appertain sounds like 'a purse-tain': the purse holds what belongs to you.
abstract.cn: appertain 听着像 a purse-tain：钱包握着属于你的东西。

examples.en: Certain duties appertain to the office of chairman.
examples.cn: 某些职责是主席职位固有的。

examples.en: Please file everything appertaining to this contract.
examples.cn: 请把与这份合同有关的一切归档。

examples.en: The honors that appertain to rank were never his goal.
examples.cn: 随地位而来的荣耀从来不是他的目标。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿婆疼」——阿婆疼谁，家产就「属于」谁，谐音仅助记，不是词源。

root: 拉丁词根 ten-/tain-（握持）：appertain 由 ap-（朝向）+ pertinere（贯穿而握）构成，本义「延伸握持到」，引申为权利、职责「握在」某身份或事项之中，即属于。

sensesIntro.en: From rights held by an owner, appertain extends to subjects related, roles and their duties, fittingness, indirect concern, membership in a system, legal incidents, and qualities and their consequences.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「权利握在所有者手中」出发，appertain 依次延伸到相关主题、职位职责、相称性、间接关涉、系统成员、法律附属以及性质与其结果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a right held firmly by its proper owner
core.cn: 核心意象：一项权利被其正当主人牢牢握住

branches.en: formal ownership: rights, offices, legal incidents
branches.cn: 正式的所有：权利、职位、法律附属

branches.en: relevance: matters and interests held in the same hand
branches.cn: 相关性：被同一只手握住的事项与利益

branches.en: what fits a thing belongs to it
branches.cn: 相称之物即属于此物

branches.en: membership held within a larger system
branches.cn: 被更大系统握住的成员身份

branches.en: qualities holding their own consequences
branches.cn: 性质握有自己的结果

intro.en: Appertain is one of dozens of English words built on the holding root tain.
intro.cn: appertain 是英语里几十个建立在「握持」词根 tain 上的词之一。

latinIntro.en: Latin tenere, to hold, is the mother root of contain, retain, tenant, and more.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tenere（握持）是 contain、retain、tenant 等词的母词根。

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「关于；属于」
同根派生，义为「切题的；相关的」

definition_zh: 地层学；层序学；考古地层；分层结构
definition_en: the study of the order, position and age of layered deposits, used in geology and archaeology to establish sequences
core_image: 一面陡壁被刮平，深浅不同的土带一层压一层，最下面的一层最老，最上面的一层最新
scene: 探方一侧的土壁被刮得平整，深浅不同的土带一层压着一层，最底下的土色最深。 The exposed wall shows stratigraphy as bands of soil stacked oldest at the bottom and youngest at the top.
sceneCN: 这里 stratigraphy 指「堆积层按上下顺序排列所构成的层序及其研究」（第 2 个义项：地层序列本身）；句意为刮平的土壁上，不同颜色的土层依次叠压，最下面的最老、最上面的最新。可辨识物件：土壁、土层带、刮刀、比例尺、层位线。

pos.zh: 地层序列；层位关系（不可数）

senses.title: The study of layered order
senses.titleCN: 地层学：研究层序的学科
senses.definition: the branch of geology and archaeology that studies how layers form, succeed and correlate
senses.definitionCN: 研究层如何形成、先后相接与对比的地质学与考古学分支
senses.example: Stratigraphy tells us which deposit formed first.
senses.exampleCN: 地层学告诉我们哪一层堆积先形成。
senses.why: Stratum is Latin for a layer spread out, from sternere, to spread; -graphy is Greek for writing, so the word means writing about layers.
senses.whyCN: stratum 是拉丁语「铺开的一层」，出自 sternere「铺展」；-graphy 是希腊语「书写」，因此这个词意为「对层的书写」。

senses.title: The layering itself
senses.definition: the actual arrangement of layers at a place, read from a section or a core
senses.definitionCN: 某地点通过剖面或岩芯读出的层的实际排列
senses.example: The stratigraphy at the trench edge is unusually clear.
senses.exampleCN: 探方边缘的层序异常清楚。
senses.why: The same word names both the discipline and its object, just as geology names both a science and a rock face.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词既指学科，也指其对象，正如 geology 既指地质学也指一处岩面。

senses.title: Archaeological stratigraphy
senses.titleCN: 考古地层：人类活动形成的堆积层序
senses.definition: the sequence of deposits made by human activity, such as floors, fills and dumps, and their cut relationships
senses.definitionCN: 由人类活动形成的堆积顺序，如居住面、填土与废弃物，及其切压关系
senses.example: Archaeological stratigraphy records a floor cut by a later pit.
senses.exampleCN: 考古地层记录了一个被后期灰坑打破的居住面。
senses.why: People also make layers, and they cut into older ones; the discipline reads both accumulation and intrusion.
senses.whyCN: 人也会制造层，并切穿更早的层；这门学科既读堆积，也读侵入。

senses.title: Correlation between sections
senses.titleCN: 地层对比：把分离的剖面接起来
senses.definition: the matching of layers across different places so that separate sequences can be joined
senses.definitionCN: 把不同地点的层相互对应，使分离的序列得以连接
senses.example: Stratigraphy links the two sides of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 地层对比把谷地两侧连接起来。
senses.why: A layer exposed in one place is not the same layer everywhere; correlation uses colour, texture and contained finds to match them.
senses.whyCN: 在一处露出的层并不等于各处的同一层；对比依靠颜色、质地与所含发现物把它们配对。

senses.title: Rock-layer geology
senses.titleCN: 岩层学：地质上的成层研究
senses.definition: the geological study of sedimentary rock layers and their ages
senses.definitionCN: 对沉积岩层及其年代的地质学研究
senses.example: Stratigraphy placed the limestone below the sandstone.
senses.exampleCN: 地层学把石灰岩定在砂岩之下。
senses.why: The discipline began with rock, not with graves; sedimentary layers accumulate in order and carry the oldest at the bottom.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科起初研究岩石，而非墓葬；沉积层按顺序堆积，最老的位于底部。

senses.title: The law of superposition
senses.titleCN: 叠加律：上覆者晚于下伏者
senses.definition: the principle that in an undisturbed sequence the upper layer is younger than the layer below it
senses.definitionCN: 在未受扰动的序列中，上层晚于其下层的原理
senses.example: Stratigraphy assumed the rule held until a burrow was found.
senses.exampleCN: 地层学一直假定这条规律成立，直到发现一处动物洞穴。
senses.why: The rule is the whole basis of relative dating, and its exceptions, such as pits and burrows, are what fieldworkers watch for.
senses.whyCN: 这条规律是相对测年的全部基础，而灰坑与洞穴等例外正是田野工作者要留意的。

senses.title: Reading a section
senses.titleCN: 判读剖面：清理剖面并绘出层界
senses.definition: the practical skill of interpreting a cleaned section and drawing its layer boundaries
senses.definitionCN: 判读清理过的剖面并绘出层界线的实践技能
senses.example: Her stratigraphy of the section was checked by a second recorder.
senses.exampleCN: 她对剖面的层序判读由第二位记录员复核。
senses.why: Layers are not labelled in the ground; the reader must decide where one ends and the next begins, and that decision is an interpretation.
senses.whyCN: 层在地下并没有标签；判读者必须决定一层在哪里结束、下一层在哪里开始，而这个决定本身就是解释。

senses.title: Layered structure as metaphor
senses.titleCN: 分层结构：比喻意义上的层次
senses.definition: any system read as stacked levels, such as a text, a society or a set of rules
senses.definitionCN: 任何被当作叠置层次来读的系统，如文本、社会或一套规则
senses.example: The historian applied stratigraphy to the layers of the law.
senses.exampleCN: 这位历史学者把分层结构用于法律的各个层次。
senses.why: Once layers mean order, the image travels: anything built up over time can be read from bottom to top.
senses.whyCN: 一旦层意味着顺序，这个意象就会迁移：任何随时间累积的东西都可以从下往上读。

intro.en: Stratigraphy joins Latin stratum, a layer, with Greek -graphia, writing. The term was coined for geology in the nineteenth century and later borrowed by archaeology. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: stratigraphy 把拉丁 stratum「层」与希腊 -graphia「书写」连在一起。这个词十九世纪为地质学而造，后来被考古学借用。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sternere meant to spread out or lay flat; its participle stratus gave stratum, a layer spread over a surface.
items.cn: sternere 意为铺开、摊平；其分词 stratus 产生 stratum，即铺在表面上的一层。

items.en: Stratum named a bed or layer, and the plural strata became the standard word for rock and soil layers.
items.cn: stratum 指一层或一层床，复数 strata 成为岩石与土壤层的标准词。

items.en: Greek graphein, to write, gave -graphia, a writing or description; geography, biography and stratigraphy all use it.
items.cn: 希腊 graphein「书写」产生 -graphia，即书写或描述；geography、biography、stratigraphy 都用它。

items.en: Geologists needed a word for the description of layered rock, and stratigraphy supplied it; the principles of superposition and correlation came with it.
items.cn: 地质学家需要一个词来描述成层岩石，stratigraphy 正好补上；叠加与对比原理随之而来。

items.en: Archaeologists borrowed the term for human deposits, adding cuts and fills to the geological vocabulary of layers.
items.cn: 考古学者把这个词借用于人类堆积，在层的地质词汇中加入切与填。

items.en: Source uncertain: the coinage is generally attributed to nineteenth-century geologists, but no single author and date are agreed, and the first use in archaeology is also undocumented.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个词的创造一般归给十九世纪的地质学家，但没有公认的单一作者与年代，它在考古学中的首次使用同样缺乏记载。

note.en: The first group holds terms from the same layer stock; the second group holds words for ordering and for layers.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「层」词干的术语；第二组是表示排序与层的词。

entries.definition: A single layer; stratigraphy is the study of many layers and their order.
entries.definitionCN: 单独的一层；stratigraphy 是研究多层及其顺序的学科。

entries.definition: Relating to stratigraphy; it describes a relationship or a position, not the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 与地层学有关的；它描述关系或位置，而非学科本身。

entries.definition: The atmospheric layer named from the same Latin word for layer, but it has nothing to do with deposits.
entries.definitionCN: 大气层名，借用了同一个拉丁「层」词，但与堆积无关。

entries.definition: The study of the earth as a whole; stratigraphy is one of its core methods.
entries.definitionCN: 研究整个地球的学科；地层学是其核心方法之一。

entries.definition: The order in which things follow one another; stratigraphy is the reading of that order in deposits.
entries.definitionCN: 事物相继出现的顺序；地层学是从堆积中读出这个顺序。

entries.definition: The layer and association in which an object lies; stratigraphy supplies the framework for context.
entries.definitionCN: 物件所在的层与共存关系；地层学为情境提供框架。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the spreading root, the writing suffix, superposition and the two-section match.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示铺展的词根、书写后缀、叠加律，以及两个剖面的对比。

normal.en: sternere, to spread, gives stratum: a layer is something spread over a surface.
normal.cn: sternere「铺展」派生 stratum：层就是铺在表面上的东西。

normal.en: -graphy is writing: stratigraphy is writing about layers.
normal.cn: -graphy 是书写：stratigraphy 就是书写层。

normal.en: Superposition: in an undisturbed stack, the top is youngest and the bottom is oldest.
normal.cn: 叠加律：在未受扰动的叠层中，最上面最新，最下面最老。

normal.en: Pits and burrows cut older layers, and those cuts must be read as later events.
normal.cn: 灰坑与洞穴切穿更老的层，这些切口必须当作更晚的事件来读。

normal.en: Correlation matches colour, texture and finds to join separate sections.
normal.cn: 对比依靠颜色、质地与发现物，把分离的剖面接起来。

abstract.en: Abstractly, stratigraphy is time made visible as order: the vertical axis is history.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，地层学是把时间变成可见的顺序：竖轴就是历史。

abstract.en: It is the art of reading interruption: what cuts what tells you what came later.
abstract.cn: 它是判读打断的技艺：谁切穿了谁，就告诉你谁更晚。

abstract.en: Any archive, text or institution built up over time can be read as a stack of layers.
abstract.cn: 任何随时间累积的档案、文本或制度，都可以当作一摞层来读。

examples.en: The pit cuts the floor, so by stratigraphy the pit is later.
examples.cn: 灰坑切穿了居住面，因此按地层关系灰坑更晚。

examples.en: Without stratigraphy, the finds would have no order at all.
examples.cn: 没有地层，这些发现物就完全没有顺序。

examples.en: The two sections were correlated by their stratigraphy.
examples.cn: 两个剖面通过地层对比被连接起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「strata（层）+ graphy（写）」——把一层层土写成一张剖面图 → 地层学

root: 拉丁 stratum「铺开的一层」（出自 sternere「铺展」）+ 希腊 -graphia「书写、描述」；字面为「对层的书写」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one stack: the discipline reads the layers, the layers themselves, human deposits, matched sections, rock strata, the rule of superposition, the act of reading and the metaphor of levels.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一叠层展开：学科读层，层本身，人类堆积，剖面对比，岩层，叠加律，判读行为，以及层次的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cleaned wall of soil, bands stacking oldest to youngest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面刮净的土壁，土带自老至新依次叠压。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE AND THE ROCK: the same reading applies to soil and to sedimentary stone.
branches.cn: 学科与岩石：同一套读法既用于土壤，也用于沉积岩。

branches.en: NATURAL AND HUMAN STACKS: people add floors, fills and cuts to the natural sequence.
branches.cn: 自然叠层与人类叠层：人在自然序列上添加居住面、填土与切口。

branches.en: JOINING SECTIONS: correlation turns separate walls into one regional sequence.
branches.cn: 连接剖面：对比把分离的土壁连成一个区域序列。

branches.en: THE RULE AND THE READING: superposition gives the logic, and the recorder applies it at the section.
branches.cn: 规律与判读：叠加律提供逻辑，记录员在剖面上应用它。

branches.en: LAYERS EVERYWHERE: once order is visible as a stack, any accumulated system can borrow the image.
branches.cn: 处处有层：一旦顺序可见为一摞，任何累积系统都能借用这个意象。

intro.en: Stratigraphy is a Latin-Greek compound, and both halves build many English technical words.
intro.cn: stratigraphy 是一个拉丁—希腊复合词，两半都构成大量英语技术词。

latinIntro.en: Latin sternere, to spread, gives stratum, stratus and stratify; Greek graphein, to write, gives -graphy, -graph and graphic. The compound names the description of layers.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sternere「铺展」衍生 stratum、stratus、stratify；希腊 graphein「书写」衍生 -graphy、-graph、graphic。这个复合词命名对层的描述。

items.structure: sternere (Latin verb, to spread out, lay flat)
items.exampleCN: sternere 衍生 stratum 与 prostration。

items.structure: stratum (Latin noun, a layer spread out)
items.example: Each stratum held a different kind of soil.
The strata dip toward the river.
items.exampleCN: 这些层向河流方向倾斜。

items.example: Water and wind stratify the sediment.
The stratified sand records repeated floods.
items.exampleCN: 分层砂记录了一次次洪水。

items.example: Stratification takes centuries in still water.
items.exampleCN: 在静水中分层需要数百年。

items.example: Graphein supplies the -graphy of many fields.

items.meaning: writing or description of a field
items.meaningCN: 某一领域的书写或描述
items.example: Geography and stratigraphy share the suffix.
items.exampleCN: geography 与 stratigraphy 共用这个后缀。

items.meaning: relating to layers or their order
items.example: The stratigraphic boundary is marked in red.

items.exampleCN: 地层专家检查了这个剖面。

definition_zh: 近亲繁殖；近交；近交衰退
definition_en: the breeding of closely related individuals, often leading to reduced fitness
core_image: 一座孤岛上的兽群多年没有外来个体加入
scene: 岛上的小种群多年没有外来个体加入。保护者警告： Inbreeding reduces the number of healthy offspring in the population.
sceneCN: 这里指「近亲繁殖」（第 1 个义项：亲缘关系很近的个体交配繁育）；句意为近亲繁殖减少了群体中健康后代的数量。

senses.title: Breeding close relatives
senses.definition: the mating of individuals that are closely related by ancestry
senses.definitionCN: 血缘关系很近的个体交配
senses.example: Inbreeding reduces the number of healthy offspring in the population.
senses.exampleCN: 近亲繁殖减少了群体中健康后代的数量。
senses.why: In- marks breeding within a closed circle, and the word names the practice that keeps relatives as parents.
senses.whyCN: in- 标记在一个封闭圈子内繁育，这个词命名让亲属成为亲本的做法。

senses.title: Inbreeding in genetics
senses.definition: the mating of individuals more closely related than the average of the population
senses.definitionCN: 亲缘关系比群体平均更近的个体交配
senses.example: The inbreeding coefficient rose to one eighth in the herd.
senses.exampleCN: 牛群的近交系数升到了八分之一。
senses.why: Genetics defines the term relative to the population average, so even a mild practice can count as inbreeding.
senses.whyCN: 遗传学以群体平均为参照定义这个术语，因此即使较温和的做法也可能算近交。

senses.title: Inbreeding depression
senses.definition: the loss of fitness and vigor caused by continued close breeding
senses.definitionCN: 持续近亲繁育造成的适合度与活力下降
senses.example: Inbreeding depression lowered the germination rate.
senses.exampleCN: 近交衰退降低了发芽率。
senses.why: The noun is often used for the harmful consequence, because hidden harmful alleles become visible when relatives mate.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词常指有害后果，因为亲属交配时隐藏的有害等位基因会显现。

senses.title: Breeding in a closed population
senses.definition: breeding within a group that has no immigration from outside
senses.definitionCN: 在没有外来个体迁入的群体内繁育
senses.example: Island populations are vulnerable to inbreeding.
senses.exampleCN: 岛屿群体容易陷入近亲繁殖。
senses.why: A closed group forces relatives to become mates, which is the structural cause of inbreeding.
senses.whyCN: 封闭群体迫使亲属成为配偶，这是近亲繁殖的结构性原因。

senses.title: Inbreeding in plants
senses.definition: self-pollination or crossing between closely related plants
senses.definitionCN: 自花授粉或亲缘很近的植株之间杂交
senses.example: Self-pollinating crops show strong inbreeding in nature.
senses.exampleCN: 自花授粉的作物在自然界表现出很强的近交。
senses.why: Plants that pollinate themselves are the extreme case: the two parents are the same individual.
senses.whyCN: 自花授粉的植物是极端情形：两个亲本就是同一个个体。

senses.title: Inbred lines in breeding
senses.definition: lines maintained by close breeding to fix traits, often used for later crossing
senses.definitionCN: 通过近亲繁育维持、以固定性状的品系，常用于后续杂交
senses.example: The lab keeps inbreeding lines for genetic studies.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室保存近交系用于遗传研究。
senses.why: Breeders sometimes use inbreeding deliberately to make uniform lines, accepting the cost in vigor.
senses.whyCN: 育种者有时有意使用近交来获得一致品系，并接受活力下降的代价。

senses.title: Marriage within a family
senses.definition: reproduction between close relatives in human populations
senses.definitionCN: 人类群体中近亲之间的生育
senses.example: Historical records document inbreeding among isolated families.
senses.exampleCN: 历史记录记载了孤立家族中的近亲通婚。
senses.why: The same biological term applies to people, where it also carries legal and social restrictions.
senses.whyCN: 同一生物术语也适用于人，但在人身上还带有法律与社会限制。

senses.title: A metaphor for a closed circle
senses.titleCN: 比喻：封闭圈子的内部循环
senses.definition: a figurative tendency of a group to draw only on itself
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体只从自身内部取材的比喻性倾向
senses.example: The studio's inbreeding of ideas made its films repetitive.
senses.exampleCN: 这家制片公司在观念上的自我循环使它的电影变得重复。
senses.why: The genetic picture of a closed group producing from itself describes any circle that stops bringing in new material.
senses.whyCN: 封闭群体只从自身繁殖的遗传图像，用来描述任何停止引入新材料的圈子。

intro.en: Inbreeding is an English compound of in- 'within' and breeding. Inbred is recorded from the late sixteenth century, the noun inbreeding from the nineteenth. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: inbreeding 是英语复合词，由 in-「在内」与 breeding 构成。inbred 的记录可追溯至 16 世纪后期，名词 inbreeding 则始于 19 世纪。年代均为约数。

items.en: The prefix in- here is the native English preposition and prefix meaning 'within', not the Latin negative in-.
items.cn: 这里的前缀 in- 是英语本族的介词与词缀，意为「在内」，而不是拉丁否定前缀 in-。

items.en: Breeding comes from Old English bredan 'to warm, cherish, produce young', and names the production of offspring.
items.cn: breeding 来自古英语 bredan「保暖、抚育、生育」，命名产生后代的过程。

items.en: The adjective inbred is recorded in the late sixteenth century, first describing animals produced within a close group.
items.cn: 形容词 inbred 在 16 世纪后期已有记录，最初描述在近亲群体内繁育的动物。

items.en: The noun inbreeding became common in the nineteenth century with pedigree breeding and the recognition of inbreeding depression.
items.cn: 名词 inbreeding 在 19 世纪随谱系育种与近交衰退的认识而常见。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest use of the noun inbreeding is dated only to the nineteenth century, and the exact first record of inbred is not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：名词 inbreeding 的最早使用只能定在 19 世纪；inbred 的确切最早记录未有定论。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same inbreed family that are easily confused; group two holds terms for related breeding strategies.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 inbreed 词族、容易混淆的形式；第二组是相关的繁育策略术语。

entries.definition: To breed close relatives; inbreeding is the process noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指让近亲繁育；inbreeding 是过程名词。

entries.definition: Produced by close breeding; it describes the result, not the practice.
entries.definitionCN: 指由近亲繁育产生的；描述结果，而非做法。

entries.definition: Breeding within one line while avoiding the closest relatives; it is a controlled compromise.
entries.definitionCN: 指在一个品系内繁育但避免最近的亲属；是有控制的折中。

entries.definition: Breeding unrelated individuals to increase diversity; it is the remedy for inbreeding.
entries.definitionCN: 指繁育无关个体以提高多样性；是近交的补救办法。

entries.definition: Breeding different lines or breeds; it brings in new alleles instead of closing the circle.
entries.definitionCN: 指让不同品系或品种繁育；引入新等位基因，而非封闭圈子。

entries.definition: Blood relationship between individuals; it is the condition that makes a mating inbreeding.
entries.definitionCN: 指个体之间的血缘关系；是使一次交配成为近亲繁殖的条件。

entries.definition: Self-pollination in plants; it is the most extreme form of inbreeding.
entries.definitionCN: 指植物的自花授粉；是近亲繁殖的最极端形式。

entries.definition: Breeding between different groups or species; it is not necessarily close breeding.
entries.definitionCN: 指不同群体或物种之间的繁育；不一定是近亲繁育。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: in- 'within' + breeding: breeding inside a closed circle.
normal.cn: in-「在内」+ breeding：在一个封闭圈子内繁育。

normal.en: The family runs inbreed, inbred, inbreeding, linebreeding, outbreeding.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 inbreed、inbred、inbreeding、linebreeding、outbreeding。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: inbreeding depression, inbreeding coefficient, avoid inbreeding.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：近交衰退、近交系数、避免近亲繁殖。

normal.en: Inbreeding is the opposite of crossbreeding: inside relatives versus outside lines.
normal.cn: 近交与杂交相对：一个是内部亲属，一个是外部世系。

normal.en: Small populations inbreed because there are no outside mates.
normal.cn: 小群体发生近交，因为没有外来配偶。

abstract.en: Picture an island herd with no new animals arriving for generations.
abstract.cn: 想象一座岛上的兽群，几代都没有新个体到来。

abstract.en: Picture a family photograph where every face resembles the last.
abstract.cn: 想象一张家族合影，每张脸都像上一张。

abstract.en: Picture a closed club that only invites its own members.
abstract.cn: 想象一个封闭俱乐部，只邀请自己的成员。

examples.en: Inbreeding depression appeared after four generations of close mating.
examples.cn: 四代近亲交配之后出现了近交衰退。

examples.en: Conservationists introduce unrelated animals to reduce inbreeding.
examples.cn: 保护工作者引入无关个体以减少近亲繁殖。

examples.en: The population avoided inbreeding by crossing with a neighboring group.
examples.cn: 这个群体通过与邻群杂交避免了近亲繁殖。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因布里丁」——只在自家圈子里找配偶，不外娶也不外嫁 → 近亲繁殖

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one closed circle: relatives become parents, and the consequences are named in genetics, conservation, crops, breeding lines, human families and metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个封闭圈子展开：亲属成为亲本，其后果再在遗传学、保护、作物、育种品系、人类家庭与比喻中获得名称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an island herd with no newcomers for generations.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座岛上的兽群，几代都没有外来者。

branches.en: PRACTICE AND DEFINITION: mating relatives, and the genetic definition relative to a population.
branches.cn: 做法与定义：亲属交配，以及相对于群体的遗传学定义。

branches.en: CONSEQUENCE AND CAUSE: depression follows, and a closed population forces it.
branches.cn: 后果与原因：衰退随之而来，封闭群体迫使它发生。

branches.en: PLANTS AND LINES: selfing is the extreme, and inbred lines are a deliberate tool.
branches.cn: 植物与品系：自交是极端，近交系是有意的工具。

branches.en: HUMAN FAMILIES: the same biology applies to people.
branches.cn: 人类家庭：同一生物学也适用于人。

branches.en: METAPHOR: any closed circle that draws only on itself.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何只从自身取材的封闭圈子。

intro.en: Inbreeding joins the native prefix in- 'within' to breeding; the prefix here is not the Latin negative in-.
intro.cn: inbreeding 把本族前缀 in-「在内」接到 breeding 上；这里的前缀不是拉丁否定前缀 in-。

latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁成分：in- 是英语本族表示「在内」的前缀，breeding 来自古英语 bredan。

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把繁育保持在群体内部。

definition_zh: 含盐的；咸的；盐水（尤指生理盐水）
definition_en: containing dissolved salt, or a prepared salt solution used in medicine
core_image: 一只挂在病床边的输液袋，透明液体里溶着与人体体液相近的盐
scene: 医院病房里，护士调整好输液袋说， The nurse replaced the saline drip before the operation.
sceneCN: 这里 saline 指「含盐的液体，尤指医用生理盐水」（第 4 个义项：生理盐水输液）；句意为：护士在手术前更换了生理盐水输液。

pos.zh: 盐水；生理盐水；（复数）盐泉、盐沼

forms.label: 比较级（技术形容词，罕用）

senses.title: Containing dissolved salt
senses.definition: containing salt dissolved in water, as a chemical property rather than a taste
senses.definitionCN: 水中溶有盐，指化学性质而非口味
senses.example: The saline groundwater lies just below the field.
senses.exampleCN: 含盐地下水就位于这块田的下方。
senses.why: Latin salinus 'of salt' adds -inus to sal 'salt', so the adjective simply marks the presence of salt in whatever it describes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 salinus「盐的」在 sal「盐」后加 -inus，因此这个形容词只是标记所描写之物含有盐。

senses.title: Tasting of salt
senses.definition: having a salty taste, said of food, drink or tears
senses.definitionCN: 带有咸味，用于食物、饮料或眼泪
senses.example: A saline tang came from the oysters, not the sauce.
senses.exampleCN: 那股咸味来自牡蛎，而不是酱汁。
senses.why: the tongue is a crude chemical detector, so the same adjective that marks dissolved salt in a lab also describes the sensation salt produces.
senses.whyCN: 舌头是一台粗略的化学探测器，因此实验室里标记溶解盐的同一个形容词，也用来描写盐带来的感觉。

senses.title: A prepared salt solution
senses.definition: water with a controlled amount of salt added, made for a specific purpose
senses.definitionCN: 按特定用途加入定量盐分的水
senses.example: Mix a saline solution to clean the wound.
senses.exampleCN: 配一份盐水溶液来清洗伤口。
senses.why: once salt is added by measure rather than found in nature, the adjective shifts from a description to a recipe.
senses.whyCN: 当盐是按量加入而非天然存在时，这个形容词就从描述变成了配方。

senses.title: The medical drip
senses.definition: a bag of salt water at body strength, given through a vein to restore fluid
senses.definitionCN: 一袋浓度与体液相近的盐水，经静脉输入以补充液体
senses.example: The nurse replaced the saline drip before the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 护士在手术前更换了生理盐水输液。
senses.why: blood is itself saline, so a solution matched to it can enter a vein without upsetting the cells; the noun shortens the full phrase.
senses.whyCN: 血液本身就是含盐的，因此浓度与之匹配的溶液能进入静脉而不扰乱细胞；名词形式是完整短语的省略。

senses.title: Salt-affected soil
senses.definition: soil in which salts have accumulated until most crops struggle
senses.definitionCN: 盐分积聚到多数作物难以生长的土壤
senses.example: Willows are among the few trees that tolerate saline soil.
senses.exampleCN: 柳树是少数能耐盐渍土的树木之一。
senses.why: the adjective attaches to the ground when irrigation or a rising water table leaves salt behind, turning a water problem into a land problem.
senses.whyCN: 当灌溉或地下水位上升把盐留下时，这个形容词就附着到土地上，把水的问题变成了地的问题。

senses.title: A salt lake
senses.definition: a lake with no outlet whose water has become far saltier than the sea
senses.definitionCN: 没有出水口、水比海咸得多的湖泊
senses.example: Nothing but algae grows in that saline lake.
senses.exampleCN: 那座盐湖里只长藻类。
senses.why: a lake that only loses water by evaporation keeps every grain of salt it receives, so the adjective marks the end point of that process.
senses.whyCN: 只靠蒸发失水的湖泊会把收到的每一粒盐都留下，因此这个形容词标记的正是这一过程的终点。

senses.title: A nasal rinse
senses.definition: a mild salt solution used to flush the nose and sinuses
senses.definitionCN: 用来冲洗鼻腔与鼻窦的淡盐水
senses.example: A warm saline rinse eased the congestion.
senses.exampleCN: 温盐水冲洗缓解了鼻塞。
senses.why: the nose lining is sensitive to concentration, so a solution close to body salt can clean it without stinging, and the adjective guarantees that strength.
senses.whyCN: 鼻黏膜对浓度敏感，接近体液盐度的溶液能清洁而不刺痛，这个形容词保证的正是这一浓度。

senses.title: An eyewash or lens rinse
senses.titleCN: 洗眼或镜片冲洗用的盐水
senses.definition: a sterile salt solution used to rinse the eye or a contact lens
senses.definitionCN: 用来冲洗眼睛或隐形眼镜的无菌盐水
senses.example: Rinse the lens in saline, never in tap water.
senses.exampleCN: 用盐水冲洗镜片，绝不要用自来水。
senses.why: tap water carries microbes and the wrong concentration, so a prepared saline keeps the eye at its own chemistry.
senses.whyCN: 自来水带有微生物且浓度不对，因此配制好的盐水能让眼睛保持自身的化学环境。

senses.title: Salt stress in plants
senses.definition: describing conditions in which too much salt in water or soil harms plants
senses.definitionCN: 水或土壤中盐分过多而伤害植物的状况
senses.example: Saline irrigation reduced the yield by a third.
senses.exampleCN: 含盐灌溉使产量减少了三分之一。
senses.why: salt outside the root pulls water out of it by osmosis, so an adjective about chemistry becomes a word about drought inside a living plant.
senses.whyCN: 根外的盐通过渗透把水从根中抽出，因此一个化学形容词变成了描述植物体内干旱的词。

intro.en: Saline comes from Latin salinus 'of salt', an adjective from sal 'salt'. English borrowed it in the seventeenth century, and the medical noun followed. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: saline 来自拉丁 salinus「盐的」，由 sal「盐」构成的形容词；英语在 17 世纪借入，医用名词随后出现。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sal 'salt' is a third-declension noun whose compounds and derivatives spread across medicine, cooking and trade.
items.cn: sal「盐」是第三变格名词，其复合词与派生词遍及医学、烹饪与贸易。

items.en: Salinus 'of salt, salty' adds -inus to the noun; the same suffix builds other quality adjectives such as marinus from mare.
items.cn: salinus「盐的、咸的」在名词后加 -inus；同一后缀也构成 marinus（由 mare「海」）等其他性质形容词。

items.en: The plural salinae named salt works and salt pans, the places where sea water was evaporated for salt.
items.cn: 复数 salinae 指盐场与盐田，即蒸发海水取盐的地方。

items.en: English took the adjective in the seventeenth century through French salin, first describing springs, wells and mineral waters.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪经法语 salin 借入这个形容词，最初用于描写泉、井与矿泉水。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the noun saline settled into medicine for a salt solution matched to body fluids, and later for the drip that carries it.
items.cn: 从 19 世纪起，名词 saline 在医学中固定指与体液匹配的盐溶液，后来又指输送它的输液。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only, not root): the earliest English citation is not firmly dated, and whether the noun entered directly from Latin or through French is generally accepted rather than proved; the Indo-European *sal- behind sal is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代，不涉及词根）：英语最早书证年代不确，名词是直接来自拉丁还是经法语传入属「一般认为是」，尚未证实；sal 背后的印欧 *sal- 为重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words built on or resembling the salt stem; group two holds words for salty water at different strengths.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在盐词干上或与之形近的词；第二组是不同浓度的咸水说法。

entries.definition: the measured amount of salt in water; saline is the adjective and salinity the quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 水中盐的测得含量；saline 是形容词，salinity 是数量。

entries.definition: a salt lake, salt pan or salt works, from Latin salinae; it names a place, not a property.
entries.definitionCN: 盐湖、盐田或盐场，来自拉丁 salinae；它指地点，不指性质。

entries.definition: from Latin sanus 'healthy': soundness of mind. The shape is close, but there is no salt in the root.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 sanus「健康的」：神志健全。词形接近，但词根中没有盐。

entries.definition: the everyday adjective for a salty taste; saline is its technical and medical counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指咸味的日常形容词；saline 是它在技术与医学语境中的对应词。

entries.definition: very salty, like brine; it often describes the sea or tears and sounds more literary than saline.
entries.definitionCN: 很咸的，如卤水；常描写海或眼泪，比 saline 更有文学色彩。

entries.definition: slightly salty because fresh and sea water have mixed; it is weaker than saline and tied to estuaries.
entries.definitionCN: 因淡水与海水混合而略带咸味；比 saline 弱，且与河口相关。

entries.definition: the substance itself, not a property; saline describes water that contains it.
entries.definitionCN: 指物质本身，而非性质；saline 描写含有这种物质的水。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin sal 'salt' plus -inus: the adjective simply says 'of salt'.
normal.cn: 拉丁 sal「盐」加 -inus：这个形容词只是说「盐的」。

normal.en: The family runs saline, salinity, salinization, salinize, desalination, salina.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 saline、salinity、salinization、salinize、desalination、salina。

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort the uses: saline solution, saline drip, saline soil, saline lake.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把用法分开：盐水溶液、生理盐水输液、盐渍土、盐湖。

normal.en: A saline drip is blood's chemistry imitated in a bag.
normal.cn: 生理盐水输液就是把血液的化学环境装进一个袋子。

normal.en: Salinae in Latin were salt works, which is why salina means a salt pan today.
normal.cn: 拉丁 salinae 是盐场，因此今天的 salina 指盐田。

abstract.en: Picture a tear that a chemist and a cook would describe with the same word.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴眼泪，化学家和厨师会用同一个词来描写它。

abstract.en: Picture a lake with no door, keeping every grain of salt it ever received.
abstract.cn: 想象一座没有出口的湖，把收到的每一粒盐都留下。

abstract.en: Picture a plant drinking from a glass it cannot reach without paying for it.
abstract.cn: 想象一株植物从一只杯子里喝水，却要为每一口付出代价。

examples.en: The clinic keeps saline solution in every treatment room.
examples.cn: 诊所的每间治疗室都备有生理盐水。

examples.en: Saline lakes form where rivers bring salt in and only evaporation takes water out.
examples.cn: 河流带入盐分、而只有蒸发带走水的地方，会形成盐湖。

examples.en: Saline groundwater limits what can be planted along the coast.
examples.cn: 含盐地下水限制了沿海可以种植的作物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「撒来盐」——把盐撒进水里，就成了盐水 → 含盐的、生理盐水

root: 拉丁 sal「盐」+ 形容词后缀 -inus → salinus「盐的、咸的」→ 法语 salin → 英语 saline；名词 saline 到 19 世纪在医学中固定为生理盐水。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses begin with a chemical presence and then move through taste, a prepared solution, the drip in a ward, salt-crusted soil, a closed lake, a rinse for nose and eye, and the stress salt puts on a living plant.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从「含有盐」这一化学事实出发，随后经过味觉、配制溶液、病房里的输液、结盐的土壤、封闭的湖泊、鼻腔与眼睛的冲洗，最后是盐给活体植物带来的胁迫。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bag of clear salt water hanging by a hospital bed, matched to the salt of blood.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只透明的盐水袋挂在病床边，浓度与血液中的盐相匹配。

branches.en: CHEMICAL PRESENCE: the adjective marks dissolved salt before any use is imagined.
branches.cn: 化学上的存在：在设想任何用途之前，这个形容词先标记溶解的盐。

branches.en: THE TONGUE'S REPORT: the same presence becomes a sensation when tasted.
branches.cn: 舌头的报告：同一种存在被尝到时，变成一种感觉。

branches.en: MADE ON PURPOSE: solution, drip, nasal rinse and eyewash are all salt water prepared to a chosen strength for a body.
branches.cn: 刻意配制：溶液、输液、鼻腔冲洗与洗眼液，都是按选定浓度为身体配制的盐水。

branches.en: WHEN IT HARMS: salt left in soil and salt outside a root both take water away.
branches.cn: 当它造成伤害：留在土里的盐与根外的盐，都会把水夺走。

branches.en: WHERE IT COLLECTS: a lake with no outlet keeps every grain and turns into brine.
branches.cn: 它汇聚之处：没有出口的湖留下每一粒盐，最终变成卤水。

intro.en: Saline is a Latin adjective with a transparent suffix; the same root also builds the nouns and compounds of water science and medicine.
intro.cn: saline 是一个后缀清晰的拉丁形容词；同一词根还构成水科学与医学中的名词与复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin sal gives salinus and salinae; English saline comes from salinus, while salina and salinity follow the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sal 衍生 salinus 与 salinae；英语 saline 来自 salinus，salina 与 salinity 则循同一词干。

items.example: Sal was weighed and taxed like a precious good.
items.exampleCN: 盐曾像贵重货物一样被称量与征税。

items.example: Salinus and marinus share the same ending.
items.exampleCN: salinus 与 marinus 共享同一词尾。

items.example: A saline spring feeds the marsh.
items.exampleCN: 一眼盐泉供给这片沼泽。

items.example: The salina produces salt by evaporation.

items.exampleCN: 盐度决定牡蛎生长的地方。
排水不良之后便是盐渍化。

items.example: Rising water salinizes the low fields.

items.exampleCN: 淡化技术让这座城得以居住。

items.example: The salimeter was calibrated at sea.
items.exampleCN: 这台盐度计在海上校准过。

latinEntries.structure: salinus, salina, salinum (adj., first and second declension)

definition_zh: n. 昏迷（状态）；（比喻）停滞不振的状态
definition_en: a state of deep unconsciousness that may last a long time
core_image: 病床上的人闭着眼，对呼唤毫无反应
scene: 车祸后他陷入昏迷，三天没有醒来。 After the crash he fell into a coma and did not wake for three days.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：coma 指昏迷；句意是车祸后他陷入昏迷，三天没有醒来。

senses.title: A deep unconscious state
senses.definition: a long state of deep unconsciousness caused by injury or illness
senses.definitionCN: 因伤或病造成的长时间深度无意识
senses.example: She was in a coma for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 她昏迷了一周。
senses.why: Greek koma means deep sleep.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 koma 意为沉睡。

senses.title: A state of inactivity
senses.definition: a figurative state in which activity has stopped
senses.definitionCN: 活动停止的比喻状态
senses.example: The town lay in a winter coma.
senses.exampleCN: 小镇陷入冬日停滞。
senses.why: Deep sleep became a picture of stillness.
senses.whyCN: 沉睡成了静止的比喻。

intro.en: Coma is the Greek word for deep sleep carried into medicine.
intro.cn: coma 是希腊语「沉睡」进入医学用语的词。

items.en: Koma means deep sleep.
items.cn: koma 意为沉睡。

items.en: English doctors use coma for unnatural sleep.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语医生用 coma 指异常沉睡。

items.en: Coma becomes a precise clinical term.
items.cn: 十九世纪 coma 成为精确的临床术语。

items.en: Intensive care manages long comas.
items.cn: 二十世纪重症监护处理长期昏迷。

items.en: The word also describes a stalled town.
items.cn: 现代也形容停滞的小镇。

note.en: The look-alike group is a near spelling; the near-meaning group names altered consciousness.
note.cn: 形近组是相近拼写；近义组列出意识改变的状态。

entries.definition: A punctuation mark.
entries.definitionCN: 逗号。

entries.definition: Fighting between forces.
entries.definitionCN: 战斗。

entries.definition: An icy body with a tail.
entries.definitionCN: 彗星。

entries.definition: The state of not being awake.
entries.definitionCN: 无意识。

entries.definition: A state of near-unconsciousness.
entries.definitionCN: 昏睡。

entries.definition: A half-conscious state.
entries.definitionCN: 恍惚。

normalIntro.en: Coma is deep sleep that will not end on its own.
normalIntro.cn: coma 是不会自行结束的沉睡。

normal.en: Koma means sleep.
normal.cn: koma 意为睡眠。

normal.en: A coma is sleep without waking.
normal.cn: coma 是不醒的睡眠。

normal.en: Doctors measure its depth.
normal.cn: 医生测量昏迷深度。

normal.en: Patients may come out of a coma.
normal.cn: 病人可能从昏迷中苏醒。

normal.en: A quiet town can be in a coma.
normal.cn: 安静小镇也可说处于停滞。

abstract.en: A room with the lights off.
abstract.cn: 熄了灯的房间。

abstract.en: Time paused inside a body.
abstract.cn: 在身体里暂停的时间。

abstract.en: Silence that lasts for days.
abstract.cn: 持续数日的沉默。

examples.en: The driver was in a coma after the accident.
examples.cn: 事故后司机陷入昏迷。

examples.en: Doctors kept him in a coma to help him heal.
examples.cn: 医生让他保持昏迷以助康复。

examples.en: The industry fell into a coma after the crash.
examples.cn: 崩盘后这个行业陷入停滞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 希腊 koma（沉睡）→ 医学 coma 昏迷，指唤不醒的深度无意识。

root: 希腊 koma（沉睡）→ 拉丁 coma → 英语 coma

sensesIntro.en: Sleeplessness in reverse: a sleep no one can wake from.
sensesIntro.cn: 与失眠相反：一个谁也唤不醒的睡眠。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a still figure in a hospital bed at night
core.cn: 核心意象：夜里病床上一动不动的身影

branches.en: A patient silent for days.
branches.cn: 数日无声的病人。

branches.en: Monitors beeping in a quiet ward.
branches.cn: 安静病房里鸣响的监护仪。

branches.en: A town with shut shutters.
branches.cn: 百叶窗紧闭的小镇。

branches.en: An economy with no movement.
branches.cn: 毫无动静的经济。

branches.en: Deep stillness in body and in place.
branches.cn: 身体与地方上的深度静止。

intro.en: Coma is a word of sleep; the list adds sleeping and numbness pieces.
intro.cn: coma 是睡眠之词；下面列出睡眠与麻木词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Greek koma is deep sleep, Latin somnus is sleep, and sopor is a stupor.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 koma 意为沉睡，拉丁语 somnus 意为睡眠，sopor 意为昏睡。

latinEntries.exampleCN: koma 产生 coma 与 comatose。
somnus 产生 insomnia 与 somnolent。
sopor 产生 soporific 与 stupor。

definition_zh: 容量大的；宽敞的；（胸怀、头脑）能容纳很多的
definition_en: able to hold much; having ample space, whether physical or mental
core_image: 一只张开口的口袋深不见底：什么都装得下
scene: 阁楼推开天窗，尘埃在光柱里浮动，四壁全被旧木箱占满。 The capacious attic swallowed decades of family clutter.
sceneCN: 这里 capacious 是「容量大的」（第 1 个义项：能装很多东西）；句意是这个宽敞的阁楼吞下了几十年的家庭杂物。

pos.zh: （心胸、头脑）宽宏的；接受力强的

derivatives.zh: 同根核心名词，义为「容量；能力；资格」
由名词加动词化后缀构成，义为「使具有资格；使有能力」（罕用）
加否定前缀构成，义为「使失去能力；使无行为能力」

senses.title: Having ample interior space
senses.definition: physically large enough inside to hold a great deal
senses.definitionCN: 内部空间足以容纳大量物品
senses.example: She loaded the capacious trunk with winter coats.
senses.exampleCN: 她往容积很大的后备箱里塞满了冬衣。
senses.why: The Latin capax means able to hold, so the literal image is a container that never fills.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 capax 意为能容纳的，字面意象就是一只总装不满的容器。

senses.title: Broad in mental grasp
senses.definition: able to take in and absorb a great deal of knowledge or experience
senses.definitionCN: 能够吸收大量知识或经验
senses.example: His capacious memory held every birthday in the village.
senses.exampleCN: 他记性极好，村里每个人的生日都记得。
senses.why: The mind is treated as a container, and a capacious one holds more before overflowing.
senses.whyCN: 心智被当作容器，容量大者在溢出之前能装下更多。

senses.title: Tolerant and embracing in outlook
senses.definition: willing to accommodate many views, people, or styles without narrowness
senses.definitionCN: 愿意容纳多种观点、人群或风格而不显狭隘
senses.example: The city's capacious culture absorbed wave after wave of newcomers.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市兼容并包的文化吸收了一波又一波新来者。
senses.why: Roominess extends from shelves and bags to attitudes and institutions.
senses.whyCN: 「空间充裕」从书架和提包延伸到态度与制度。

intro.en: Capacious comes from Latin capax, able to hold much, from capere, to take or seize, one of the most productive roots in Latin.
intro.cn: capacious 来自拉丁语 capax（能容纳许多的），词根 capere（拿取、抓住）是拉丁语中最高产的词根之一。

items.en: The root *kap- means to grasp or seize, seen in have and heave.
items.cn: 词根 *kap- 意为抓住、握取，英语 have、heave 亦与之相关。

items.en: Latin capere meant to take, seize, or hold; its adjective capax meant roomy and receptive.
items.cn: 拉丁语 capere 意为拿取、抓住、容纳；其形容词 capax 意为宽敞的、善于接纳的。

items.en: English took capacious from French forms in the seventeenth century for physical roominess first.
items.cn: 英语于十七世纪经法语借入 capacious，最初用于形容物理空间的宽敞。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the mental sense was common, praising capacious memories and minds.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，心智义已很常见，用来称赞博闻强记与开阔的头脑。

items.en: Today it prefers grand containers: bags, halls, memories, and civic cultures.
items.cn: 如今它偏爱形容大容器：提包、大厅、记忆与城市文化。

note.en: Capacious heads a family of hold-words stretching from capture to capacity.
note.cn: capacious 是「容纳」词族之首，从 capture 一路延伸到 capacity。

entries.definition: The amount that can be held, or the ability to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 容量；能力；资格。

entries.definition: One who has been taken and held, from the seize root.
entries.definitionCN: 俘虏；被捉住的人，出自「抓取」词根。

entries.definition: Given to faultfinding; looks and sounds close but means critical rather than roomy.
entries.definitionCN: 吹毛求疵的，形近音近，义为「爱挑刺」而非「容量大」。

entries.definition: A large flightless bird; purely coincidental sound resemblance.
entries.definitionCN: 食火鸡，与 capacious 只是发音偶然相似。

entries.definition: Having ample space, emphasizing openness over holding power.
entries.definitionCN: 宽敞的，侧重开阔而非装载力。

entries.definition: Having plenty of room, everyday register.
entries.definitionCN: 空间宽裕的，日常用语。

entries.definition: Spreading out widely, or generous in manner.
entries.definitionCN: 辽阔的；（人）开朗豪爽的。

entries.definition: Conveniently and amply spacious.
entries.definitionCN: 宽敞便利的，正式用语。

entries.definition: Confined and uncomfortably small.
entries.definitionCN: 狭窄局促的，是 capacious 的反义对照。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the hold root and the never-full container.
normalIntro.cn: 五条围绕「容纳」词根与「装不满的容器」的记忆钩子。

normal.en: Root core: Latin capere, to take and hold, is the same root in capture and captive.
normal.cn: 词根核心：拉丁语 capere（拿取、容纳）也是 capture、captive 的词根。

normal.en: Adjective engine: capax plus -ious gives capacious, just as audax gives audacious.
normal.cn: 形容词引擎：capax 加 -ious 得 capacious，正如 audax 加 -ious 得 audacious。

normal.en: Noun home: the plain noun of the family is capacity, the amount it holds.
normal.cn: 名词归宿：词族的普通名词是 capacity，即容纳量。

normal.en: Trap guard: captious means faultfinding, not roomy; never confuse the pair.
normal.cn: 陷阱防守：captious 是吹毛求疵，不是容量大，切勿混淆。

normal.en: Upgrade pair: capacious is spacious with ambition, saved for big bags and bigger minds.
normal.cn: 升级搭配：capacious 是胸怀大志的 spacious，专配大包与更大的头脑。

abstract.en: A carpetbag that seems bottomless, accepting coat after coat without complaint.
abstract.cn: 一只仿佛没有底的旅行袋，一件接一件地吞下大衣毫无怨言。

abstract.en: A library whose aisles keep folding into new shelves as you walk.
abstract.cn: 一座越走越深的图书馆，书架随脚步不断折叠出新。

abstract.en: A harbor at dusk holding ships of every flag without a ripple of complaint.
abstract.cn: 黄昏的港口，悬挂万国旗的船只静静停泊，波澜不惊。

examples.en: The stadium's capacious bowl absorbed the rain-soaked crowd.
examples.cn: 体育场容量巨大的看台装下了浑身湿透的人群。

examples.en: Her capacious curiosity ranged from beetles to symphonies.
examples.cn: 她求知欲极强，从甲虫到交响乐无所不涉。

examples.en: The novel needs a capacious reader willing to hold ten plots at once.
examples.cn: 这部小说需要一位胸怀宽广、能同时容纳十条情节线的读者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克配顺」——什么都能克化、都能配上、都能顺进肚里，正是容量超大、来者不拒；联想一只永远装不满的大口袋。

root: 源自拉丁语 capax（能容纳的），词根 capere（拿取、抓住、容纳），可上溯至印欧词根 *kap-（抓取）。同根词极多：capacity（容量）、captive（俘虏）、capture（捕获）、capture 与 accept、concept 皆含此根。十七世纪经法语进入英语，先表物理容积，后扩展至心智与胸襟。

sensesIntro.en: From roomy containers the word grows into capacious minds and tolerant cultures.
sensesIntro.cn: 从宽敞的容器出发，词义生长为博大的头脑与兼容的文化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a container that never fills, accepting whatever arrives.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只永远装不满的容器，来者不拒。

branches.en: THE WAREHOUSE: bags, trunks, and halls that swallow cargo.
branches.cn: 仓库：吞下货物的提包、箱柜与大厅。

branches.en: THE STUDY: memories and intellects that hold whole libraries.
branches.cn: 书房：装下整座图书馆的记忆与才智。

branches.en: THE HARBOR: cultures making room for every arrival.
branches.cn: 港口：为每个到来者留出位置的文化。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: capacity as the noun that quantifies the adjective.
branches.cn: 度量：capacity 是给这个形容词定量的名词。

branches.en: THE VIRTUE: roominess of mind praised as generosity.
branches.cn: 美德：心灵的宽敞被赞为慷慨。

intro.en: Capacious is the Latin stem cap- plus the adjective ending -acious, literally much-holding.
intro.cn: capacious 由拉丁词干 cap- 加形容词词尾 -acious 构成，字面即「能容纳很多的」。

latinIntro.en: The capere root is a Latin engine room, powering dozens of English words about taking and holding.
latinIntro.cn: capere 词根是拉丁语的发动机室，驱动着英语中数十个关于拿取与容纳的词。

items.exampleCN: 拿在手中（拉丁语用例示意）。
能容万物（拉丁语用例示意）。

latinEntries.exampleCN: 善于接纳的心智（拉丁语用例示意）。

definition_zh: v. 减去；扣除（款项、分数等）
definition_en: to take away an amount or part from a total
core_image: 一张工资单上，总额下面划掉几行，剩下的才是到手的数
scene: 会计从总额里扣掉税款。 They deduct tax from the total.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：deduct 指从总额中扣除；句意是他们从总额里扣掉税款。

senses.title: Take money off a total
senses.definition: to remove an amount of money from a total
senses.definitionCN: 从总额中去掉一笔钱
senses.example: They deduct tax from the total.
senses.exampleCN: 他们从总额里扣掉税款。
senses.why: A line crossed out on a pay slip.
senses.whyCN: 工资单上被划掉的一行。

senses.title: Take away points or marks
senses.definition: to remove points or marks as a penalty
senses.definitionCN: 作为处罚去掉分数
senses.example: The judge deducted two points.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判扣掉了两分。
senses.why: A score lowered by a written stroke.
senses.whyCN: 一笔划下去，分数就低了。

senses.title: Subtract in arithmetic
senses.definition: to take one number away from another
senses.definitionCN: 从一个数里去掉另一个数
senses.example: Deduct the discount before you pay.
senses.exampleCN: 付款前先减去折扣。
senses.why: A pile made smaller by removing some.
senses.whyCN: 拿走一些，堆就变小了。

intro.en: Deduct comes from Latin deducere, to lead away, from de- plus ducere, to lead.
intro.cn: deduct 源自拉丁语 deducere（领走），由 de- 加 ducere（引领）构成。

items.en: Ducere meant to lead.
items.cn: ducere 意为引领。

items.en: Deducere meant to lead away or draw down.
items.cn: deducere 意为领走或往下引。

items.en: Deductus was the past participle of deducere.
items.cn: deductus 是 deducere 的过去分词。

items.en: Deduct entered English for taking away an amount.
items.cn: 十五世纪 deduct 以扣除数额义进入英语。

items.en: Deduct also carried the sense of inferring.
items.cn: 十六世纪 deduct 也带有推断的含义。

items.en: Deduct settled on the money sense in accounts.
items.cn: 十九世纪 deduct 在账目上固定为扣款义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the duct- leading root; the near-meaning group names taking away.
note.cn: 形近组共享 duct-（引领）词根；近义组都是「拿走一部分」的说法。

entries.definition: To reach a conclusion by reasoning.
entries.definitionCN: 推断。

entries.definition: To lead or carry something through.
entries.definitionCN: 引导；传导。

entries.definition: To bring someone into a position or group.
entries.definitionCN: 引入；使就职。

entries.definition: To take a number or amount away from another.
entries.definitionCN: 减去。

entries.definition: To take something away from a place.
entries.definitionCN: 去掉；移除。

entries.definition: An amount taken off the usual price.
entries.definitionCN: 折扣。

entries.definition: To keep back money or information.
entries.definitionCN: 扣留；保留。

normalIntro.en: Deduct is de- plus ducere, to lead: lead an amount away from the total.
normalIntro.cn: deduct 就是 de- 加 ducere（引领）：把一笔数额从总额里领走。

normal.en: Ducere means to lead.
normal.cn: ducere 意为引领。

normal.en: De- means away.
normal.cn: de- 表示离开。

normal.en: Deduct leads money away.
normal.cn: deduct 把钱领走。

normal.en: A pay slip shows the deducted line.
normal.cn: 工资单上能看到被扣掉的那一行。

normal.en: The total gets smaller.
normal.cn: 总额变小了。

abstract.en: A line crossed out on a pay slip.
abstract.cn: 工资单上被划掉的一行。

abstract.en: A score lowered by a written stroke.
abstract.cn: 一笔划下去，分数就低了。

abstract.en: A pile made smaller by removing some.
abstract.cn: 拿走一些，堆就变小了。

examples.en: The bank deducted a service fee.
examples.cn: 银行扣除了一笔服务费。

examples.en: We deduct the deposit from the final bill.
examples.cn: 我们从最终账单里扣除定金。

examples.en: Ten marks were deducted for lateness.
examples.cn: 因迟到被扣了十分。

dict_mnemonic.text: deduct 谐音「弟大克特」——不如记 de（离开）＋ duct（引导，与 conduct 同根）＝把一笔钱引导出去，「扣除、减去」。

root: 拉丁语 ducere（引领）→ deducere（领走）→ deductus → 英语 deduct

sensesIntro.en: One crossed-out line: money, points and numbers.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一道划掉的线：钱、分数与数字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line crossed out on a pay slip so the total shrinks
core.cn: 核心意象：工资单上划掉一行，总额随之变小

branches.en: A line crossed out on a pay slip.
branches.cn: 工资单上被划掉的一行。

branches.en: A score lowered by a written stroke.
branches.cn: 一笔划下去，分数就低了。

branches.en: A pile made smaller by removing some.
branches.cn: 拿走一些，堆就变小了。

branches.en: Both remove a counted amount as a charge or penalty.
branches.cn: 两者都作为费用或处罚去掉一个可计数的量。

branches.en: Both make a total smaller by taking a part away.
branches.cn: 两者都通过拿走一部分让总额变小。

intro.en: Deduct is de- plus ducere; the leading root builds many direction words.
intro.cn: deduct 由 de- 加 ducere 构成；引领这个词根造出许多方向类词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere means to lead and trahere means to draw.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ducere 意为引领，trahere 意为拉。
